records.description:
**Description**
Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Department: EHSQ / Quality
 
 
Location: Houston, TX
 
 
Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality
 
 
Direct Reports: None
 
 
FLSA Status: Exempt
 
 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time
 
 
Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote
 
 
Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.
 
 
The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.
 
 
**Summary**
The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on high-voltage, substation, and transmission construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on HV and substation scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers collector substations, switchyards and points of interconnection, and generation tie-lines (gen-tie); medium-voltage collection systems remain within the scope of Electrical Quality.
 
 
The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active HV, substation, or gen-tie construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of HV and substation Quality across the portfolio.
 
 
Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors, combined with the judgment to translate engineering, utility, manufacturer, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and Transmission & Distribution (T&D) teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, relay and protection settings, and functional commissioning remain with Engineering and Commissioning; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.
 
 
This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.
 
 
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time."
 
 
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Serve as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on HV, substation, switchyard, point of interconnection, and gen-tie construction, supporting the Senior Director of Quality and the Regional Quality Managers.
* Develop, own, and maintain company-standard ITP templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, SWIs, and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) content for HV and substation scopes, ensuring they reflect current engineering standards, manufacturer requirements, utility requirements, and lessons learned.
* Build and maintain HV and substation inspection templates and workflows in Procore, in coordination with Quality Systems, so that discipline inspections are performed and recorded consistently across all projects.
* Integrate with the assigned Regional Quality Manager on each project containing HV, substation, or gen-tie scope, from pre-mobilization planning through turnover, confirming discipline requirements are incorporated into the Site-Specific Quality Management Plan (SSQMP), ITPs, inspection staffing plan, and inspection schedule.
* Support the Preconstruction Quality SME by tailoring discipline ITPs and checklists for project kickoff packages and identifying HV and substation-specific contract, utility, testing, and special inspection requirements.
* Provide technical direction to the HV & Substation Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors assigned to projects, in coordination with the Site Quality Manager, who retains administrative supervision and day-to-day site direction.
* Participate in recruitment, technical interviewing, onboarding, and qualification of discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, and provide performance input to the Site Quality Manager and Regional Quality Manager.
* Develop and deliver discipline-specific training for Quality personnel, covering acceptance criteria, inspection methods, documentation requirements, and common HV and substation failure modes.
* Conduct scheduled jobsite visits to verify implementation of the HV and substation Quality program, perform surveillance of field inspection activities, and audit discipline records in Procore for accuracy, completeness, traceability, and objective evidence.
* Provide technical review and approval of subcontractor Quality Control Plans, ITPs, and inspection forms for HV, substation, and gen-tie scopes prior to acceptance by the Site Quality Manager, and verify subcontractor Quality performance through surveillance and audit.
* Provide technical review and concurrence on proposed repair and use-as-is dispositions for nonconformances within the discipline, and on other dispositions as requested by the Site Quality Manager, in coordination with Engineering.
* Lead or support root cause analysis for significant or recurring HV and substation nonconformances, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure across the portfolio.
* Exercise stop-work authority for quality-driven conditions in accordance with company policy, coordinating through the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact on site.
* Elevate unresolved technical disagreements with site Quality, Construction, or subcontractor personnel to the Regional Quality Manager and Senior Director of Quality, with a documented position and recommended resolution.
* Define Quality’s verification requirements for receiving, storage, preservation, handling, and installation of major HV equipment, including power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, and control enclosures, in alignment with manufacturer requirements.
* Review acceptance test records and third-party test reports for completeness and conformance with ANSI/NETA ATS, project specifications, and manufacturer requirements, and coordinate Quality witness points with testing agencies and Commissioning.
* Define and support Quality’s responsibilities within the functional testing and cold commissioning RACI and in energization-readiness and turnover verification for HV and substation systems, while maintaining clear separation from relay settings, protection coordination, and functional commissioning responsibilities.
* Where required by contract and as directed by the Senior Director of Quality, support factory acceptance test (FAT) witnessing and source inspection of major HV equipment, and contribute to the development of a formal source inspection program as the organization establishes one.
* Coordinate with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, and third-party agencies on HV and substation Quality matters, including utility inspection and witness requirements for facilities built to utility standards.
* Align closely with the Engineering and T&D teams to resolve technical questions, participate in design and constructability reviews, and maintain consistent acceptance criteria across projects.
* Monitor HV and substation Quality KPIs and nonconformance trends across the portfolio, and report findings, emerging risks, and recommendations to the Senior Director of Quality.
* Provide input on discipline staffing and resource planning, including the number and qualification of Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors and third-party testing needs, for estimating and project staffing plans.
* Define the HV and substation Quality records required for turnover and verify completeness of discipline turnover documentation.
* Capture lessons learned from executed projects and incorporate them into discipline templates, training, and the broader Quality Management System (QMS).
* Interact and collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, T&D, Construction, Commissioning, Subcontract Management, and Safety teams to embed Quality into project execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned.
* Travel is required up to 50%, including scheduled jobsite visits, extended site visits, short-notice trips, and overnight stays.

**Key Competencies / Core Skills**

* Recognized technical authority who guides others through credibility and clear reasoning rather than positional authority.
* Translates engineering, manufacturer, utility, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria.
* Builds standardized tools, including ITPs, checklists, SWIs, and Procore templates, that scale across projects, regions, and delivery models.
* Leads effectively within a matrixed structure, supporting the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact while holding the technical standard for the discipline.
* Holds the standard under schedule and commercial pressure while maintaining professional, collaborative working relationships.
* Understands the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, electrical testing, protection and control, and Commissioning, and escalates appropriately.
* Maintains exceptional attention to detail across inspection records, test reports, and supporting objective evidence.
* Analyzes deficiency trends across the portfolio and translates findings into durable process change.
* Communicates clearly and factually with field personnel, engineers, utilities, owners, and executive leadership, both in writing and in person.
* Coaches and develops discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, treating development of the bench as a core responsibility.
* Manages multiple concurrent projects, travel demands, and shifting priorities while maintaining accountability.
* Maintains composure and a solutions-focused approach under pressure, disagreement, and challenging field conditions.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive quality experience in utility-scale renewable-energy, utility, substation, transmission, or industrial electrical construction, including at least 5 years of direct Quality responsibility on high-voltage substation or transmission projects; utility-scale PV electrical experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
* At least 5 years in a quality leadership or management role, including directing inspection personnel or leading Quality programs across multiple projects.
* Demonstrated experience authoring and maintaining ITPs, Quality Inspection Checklists, Standard Work Instructions, and procedures for HV and substation construction.
* Strong working knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, station service equipment, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors.
* Demonstrated ability to read and apply IFC drawings, one-line and three-line diagrams, grounding plans, physical arrangement drawings, schematics and wiring diagrams, cable schedules, specifications, approved submittals, and manufacturer instructions.
* Experience reviewing electrical acceptance test documentation and third-party test reports against ANSI/NETA ATS and project specifications.
* Experience overseeing Quality on both self-performed and subcontracted HV and substation work, including review of subcontractor Quality Control Plans and ITPs.
* Experience coordinating Quality activities with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, testing agencies, and equipment manufacturers.
* Demonstrated experience with nonconformance management, root cause analysis methodology (5-Why, fishbone, fault tree, or equivalent), and corrective action programs.
* Demonstrated understanding of the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, protection and control, and Commissioning responsibilities.
* Proficiency with Procore (Quality & Field Management modules) and SharePoint.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
* Ability to work remotely with a reliable high-speed internet connection and flexibility to support projects across Eastern through Pacific Time Zones as required.
* Must hold and maintain a valid U.S. driver’s license and have the ability to safely operate a motor vehicle, including the ability to rent vehicles for business travel without restrictions that would interfere with job performance.
* Ability to successfully pass a motor vehicle/driving record background check in accordance with company policy.
* Must be able to pass pre-employment, regular, and random drug and alcohol screenings in compliance with company and customer requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional certifications such as:

+ American Society for Quality (ASQ): Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Construction Quality Manager (CCQM), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA)
+ InterNational Electrical Testing Association (NETA): NETA Certified Technician, Level III or Level IV
+ American Welding Society (AWS): Certified Welding Inspector (CWI)
+ American Concrete Institute (ACI): Concrete Field Testing Technician, Grade I
+ Electrical licensing: State journeyman or master electrician license
+ Project Management Institute (PMI): Project Management Professional (PMP)

* Experience witnessing factory acceptance testing or performing source inspection of power transformers, circuit breakers, switchgear, or control enclosures.
* Experience across multiple substation configurations, voltage classes, and equipment manufacturers, including facilities built to interconnecting utility standards and transferred to utility ownership.
* Experience with gen-tie transmission line construction, including foundations, steel structures, conductor and OPGW installation, and associated hardware.
* Working knowledge of NESC (IEEE C2), NEC (NFPA 70), ANSI/NETA ATS, IEEE 80, and IEEE C57 series standards for power transformers.
* Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and formal Quality Management System requirements.
* Experience developing and delivering technical training for Quality or field personnel.
* Advanced proficiency with Procore, including inspection template configuration, reporting, and workflow design, as well as Power BI.
* Experience supporting utility-scale solar PV and BESS projects with integrated substation and interconnection scopes.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish, with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse project teams.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
 
 

* Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while operating a computer and reviewing documentation, drawings, and test records.
* Ability to effectively exchange accurate information in verbal and written form with employees, contractors, utilities, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to conduct regular jobsite visits requiring extended standing and walking on uneven or unpaved terrain, as well as bending, stooping, kneeling, and climbing stairs or ladders to access substation and HV construction areas.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds of inspection equipment, documentation, or other work-related materials as required.
* Ability to perform field activities while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, and arc-rated clothing or other project-specific PPE where required.
* Ability to safely access substation and HV construction areas in accordance with site safety requirements, electrical safe-work practices, qualification requirements, and access controls.
* Ability to travel domestically up to 50% of the time, including by air, with flexibility for short-notice trips, overnight stays, and extended site visits.
* Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
 
 

* Work is divided between a remote/home office environment, requiring reliable high-speed internet and standard office equipment, including audio/video conferencing, and active construction sites.
* Field work is performed at utility-scale substation, high-voltage, gen-tie, solar, and BESS construction sites, where conditions may include outdoor weather exposure, dust, moderate to high noise levels, moving construction equipment, and uneven terrain. Appropriate PPE will be provided and required.
* Field work regularly occurs in proximity to energized or potentially energized facilities as projects progress toward energization, requiring strict adherence to electrical safety requirements, qualification boundaries, and access controls.
* Work schedules during jobsite visits may vary based on construction activities, testing schedules, utility requirements, and project milestones, and may include early starts, extended hours, or weekends.
* Regular interaction with cross-functional teams in both virtual and in-person settings, requiring adaptability to both independent and collaborative work environments.

records.description:
**About Rivian**
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
 
 
As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
 
 
**Role Summary**
As a leader of a multi-disciplinary team of manufacturing engineers, you will be instrumental in launching new products and capacities at Rivian, transforming innovative ideas into tangible realities. This role sits at the intersection of product design, validation, factory design, and launch, ultimately delivering Rivian's best ideas into the hands of our customers. You will be responsible for leading and developing a motivated team of manufacturing SMEs in supporting all Rivian vehicle products and factories. This position is located at our Plymouth, MI headquarters or Georgia facility and will require significant travel to our manufacturing facilities in Normal, IL, and future locations. This role reports directly to the Director of Manufacturing Engineering in General Assembly.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Lead a team of manufacturing engineers responsible for designing and executing workstation design aligned with lean manufacturing principles. Workstation design supports overall plant metrics of 90 - 95% utilization and greater than 50 value added elements. Start to finish ownership of workstation design from virtual build through launch.
* Support Rivian manufacturing lines and sites and cover factory layout, manufacturing technology selection, equipment design, process design, etc.
* A special focus of this team will be advancing Rivian’s manufacturing technology and innovation roadmap
* Conduct virtual builds, support design validation builds of next generation products and provide Design for Manufacturing and Assembly feedback, collaborating with vehicle architecture, design, software, and other upstream partners
* Define and execute launch and ramp strategies, collaborating with launch, operations, RPS, quality and design responsible teams
* Deliver production documentation such as JES, PFMEA, Control Plans etc.
* Develop and implement processes, standards and workflows to improve team efficiency
* Actively mentor and grow manufacturing engineers and managers through technical leadership, translate vision into action, inspiring from ideation to execution
* Actively engage in value engineering, challenge assumptions and break the status quo

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering or similar technical field.
* 10+ years of experience in an engineering role related to manufacturing engineering, DFMA, product optimization, manufacturing process or equipment development
* Expertise in manufacturing and industrial engineering principles (OEE, cycle time analysis, DVA, Cp/Cpk, GR&R, ergonomics, DOE, quality control, equipment selection, ROI, error proofing, supply chain & logistics)
* Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems using first principles, challenge assumptions and biased towards action
* Proven technical leader that can lead and influence cross-functional teams launching new products, lean manufacturing workstations and material flow processes
* Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, ability to concisely summarize and escalate complex topics
* Experienced working within 2D & 3D CAD environments, simulation tools and other digital tools in the field of engineering

**Pay Disclosure**
The salary range for this role is $161,000-$201,200 for Georgia and Michigan based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
 
 
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.
 
 
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.
 
 
You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than 1/1/2027.
 
 
**Interview Integrity & AI Policy**
Our interview process is designed to evaluate your personal technical foundation, real-time problem-solving logic, and structured capabilities. Therefore,
**the use of assistive generative AI tools to formulate or deliver your solutions during live interview sessions is not permitted**
. We care most about how you think — how you make sense of unclear requirements, weigh trade-offs, and explain why you chose one approach over another. We value your unique human perspective, your authenticity, and the journey it takes to reach a solution.
 
 
**Equal Opportunity**
Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.
 
 
Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.
 
 
**Candidate Data Privacy and Technology**
Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.
 
 
Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.
 
 
Rivian may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.
 
 
How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Rivian uses iCIMS Talent Cloud Artificial Intelligence (TCAI) and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.
 
 
AI does not make hiring decisions: Qualified candidate applications are reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.
 
 
Participation in AI profile matching is entirely voluntary. If you prefer that your profile not be used in this process, you can opt out at any time. Opting out means your profile will be excluded from automated matching and will not be surfaced for additional roles through this system. Your current application remains active and will not be affected in any way.
 
 
**Please note that we are currently not accepting applications from third party application services.**

records.description:
**About Rivian**
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
 
 
As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
 
 
**Role Summary**
As a leader of a multi-disciplinary team of manufacturing engineers, you will be instrumental in launching new products and capacities at Rivian, transforming innovative ideas into tangible realities. This role sits at the intersection of product design, validation, factory design, and launch, ultimately delivering Rivian's best ideas into the hands of our customers. You will be responsible for leading and developing a motivated team of manufacturing SMEs in supporting all Rivian vehicle products and factories. This position is located at our Plymouth, MI headquarters or Georgia facility and will require significant travel to our manufacturing facilities in Normal, IL, and future locations. This role reports directly to the Director of Manufacturing Engineering in General Assembly.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Lead a team of manufacturing engineers responsible for designing and executing workstation design aligned with lean manufacturing principles. Workstation design supports overall plant metrics of 90 - 95% utilization and greater than 50 value added elements. Start to finish ownership of workstation design from virtual build through launch.
* Support Rivian manufacturing lines and sites and cover factory layout, manufacturing technology selection, equipment design, process design, etc.
* A special focus of this team will be advancing Rivian’s manufacturing technology and innovation roadmap
* Conduct virtual builds, support design validation builds of next generation products and provide Design for Manufacturing and Assembly feedback, collaborating with vehicle architecture, design, software, and other upstream partners
* Define and execute launch and ramp strategies, collaborating with launch, operations, RPS, quality and design responsible teams
* Deliver production documentation such as JES, PFMEA, Control Plans etc.
* Develop and implement processes, standards and workflows to improve team efficiency
* Actively mentor and grow manufacturing engineers and managers through technical leadership, translate vision into action, inspiring from ideation to execution
* Actively engage in value engineering, challenge assumptions and break the status quo

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering or similar technical field.
* 10+ years of experience in an engineering role related to manufacturing engineering, DFMA, product optimization, manufacturing process or equipment development
* Expertise in manufacturing and industrial engineering principles (OEE, cycle time analysis, DVA, Cp/Cpk, GR&R, ergonomics, DOE, quality control, equipment selection, ROI, error proofing, supply chain & logistics)
* Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems using first principles, challenge assumptions and biased towards action
* Proven technical leader that can lead and influence cross-functional teams launching new products, lean manufacturing workstations and material flow processes
* Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, ability to concisely summarize and escalate complex topics
* Experienced working within 2D & 3D CAD environments, simulation tools and other digital tools in the field of engineering

**Pay Disclosure**
The salary range for this role is $161,000-$201,200 for Georgia and Michigan based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
 
 
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.
 
 
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.
 
 
You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than 1/1/2027.
 
 
**Interview Integrity & AI Policy**
Our interview process is designed to evaluate your personal technical foundation, real-time problem-solving logic, and structured capabilities. Therefore,
**the use of assistive generative AI tools to formulate or deliver your solutions during live interview sessions is not permitted**
. We care most about how you think — how you make sense of unclear requirements, weigh trade-offs, and explain why you chose one approach over another. We value your unique human perspective, your authenticity, and the journey it takes to reach a solution.
 
 
**Equal Opportunity**
Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.
 
 
Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.
 
 
**Candidate Data Privacy and Technology**
Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.
 
 
Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.
 
 
Rivian may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.
 
 
How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Rivian uses iCIMS Talent Cloud Artificial Intelligence (TCAI) and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.
 
 
AI does not make hiring decisions: Qualified candidate applications are reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.
 
 
Participation in AI profile matching is entirely voluntary. If you prefer that your profile not be used in this process, you can opt out at any time. Opting out means your profile will be excluded from automated matching and will not be surfaced for additional roles through this system. Your current application remains active and will not be affected in any way.
 
 
**Please note that we are currently not accepting applications from third party application services.**

records.title: Sr. Manager Manufacturing Engineer
records.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
DESCRIPTION:
 
 
As a Sr. Manager, Manufacturing Engineering at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will guide and support engineering teams to drive operational excellence and innovation across our manufacturing facilities. You will provide strategic direction and technical leadership for manufacturing processes, automation initiatives, and continuous improvement projects while ensuring compliance with quality and regulatory requirements. Working collaboratively with cross-functional teams, you'll optimize production efficiency, implement new technologies, and deliver solutions that enable our mission of making the world healthier, cleaner and safer.
 
 
REQUIREMENTS:
 
 

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in regulated manufacturing environments (pharmaceutical, medical device, or related industries)
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Chemical) or related technical field. Strong focus on Automation required.
* Industry certifications in Six Sigma, PMP, or related areas are beneficial
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical teams and facilitating organizational change
* Demonstrated success implementing automation, digitalization and continuous improvement initiatives
* Strong understanding of cGMP, ISO standards and regulatory compliance requirements
* Experience with new product introductions, technology transfers and process validation
* Expertise in lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodology and practical process improvements (PPI)
* Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic plans aligned with business objectives
* Strong project management skills and experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities with data-driven decision making
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills to engage stakeholders at all levels
* Proficiency with manufacturing systems, automation platforms and quality tools
* Ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
* Experience with capital project planning, budgeting and resource allocation
* Relocation: Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
* Work Authorization: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer-sponsored work authorization.
* Pre-Employment Screening: Employment is contingent upon successful completion of all applicable pre-employment requirements, including a background check and drug screening, in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

**Compensation And Benefits**
The salary range estimated for this position based in New Jersey is $155,100.00–$232,650.00.
 
 
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
 
 

* A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
* Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
* At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
* Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
* Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

records.title: Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Propulsion)
records.description:
**About Varda**
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
**Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.**
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
 
 
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
 
 
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
 
 
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
 
 
**About This Role**
As the
**Principal Propulsion Manufacturing Engineer**
at Varda, you will have the opportunity to utilize your experience to scale manufacturing from a few bespoke vehicles to many consistent, concurrent builds. This role supports propulsion system production, including valve assembly, tube fabrication, pressure vessel integration, and engine integration. The Propulsion ME owns manufacturing processes for high-pressure fluid systems and propulsion hardware from tube shop operations through acceptance testing. Manufacturing Engineers are a vital part of increasing Varda's build cadence, working directly with design engineers and technicians across the full range of processes required to manufacture our vehicles. The focus of the job is to implement incremental improvement for every vehicle Varda produces.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Own end-to-end manufacturing processes for propulsion system production: valve assembly, tube fabrication, pressure vessel integration, and engine integration
* Develop and maintain work instructions, process traveler documents, and process specifications for high-pressure fluid systems and propulsion hardware
* Provide technical direction to improve propulsion build processes and drive increased vehicle production cadence
* Implement and enforce propulsion-specific cleanliness protocols, contamination control procedures, and propellant compatibility requirements
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions (RCCA) for propulsion non-conformances, including leak events, contamination findings, and assembly defects
* Define tooling and test equipment requirements for tube shop operations, leak checks, and propulsion acceptance testing
* Collaborate with design engineers and supply chain to prevent schedule delays and resolve incoming hardware quality issues
* Refine propulsion work cell layouts and product flow to support cadence increase and concurrent vehicle builds

**Basic Qualifications**

* B.S. in Mechanical, Manufacturing, or a related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience (typically 6–10+ years)
* 6+ years of manufacturing experience with propulsion systems, fluid systems, or high-pressure hardware in aerospace or a related industry
* Hands-on experience with tube fabrication, tube bending, tube fitting installation, and high-pressure fluid system assembly
* Familiarity with propulsion system cleanliness requirements, cleanliness verification methods, and contamination control procedures
* Experience reading and interpreting engineering drawings, P&IDs, and assembly models for fluid systems
* Strong first principles problem-solving capability; able to diagnose propulsion build defects and drive corrective action to closure
* Must be physically able to regularly lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, and stand for extended periods while working directly with flight hardware

**Preferred Skills And Experience**

* M.S. degree in Mechanical engineering specialized in Fluid Mechanics, Process Engineering, or related discipline
* Experience manufacturing and assembling propulsion systems for launch vehicles, spacecraft, or hypersonic vehicles, including valve assembly and pressure vessel integration
* Experience with high pressure fluid systems testing, or qualification of assemblies including energetics and explosives.
* Experience with materials including metals, composites, and plastics for use in propulsion systems.
* Experience with manufacturing methods relevant to propulsion systems, including welding, orbital welding, machining and additive manufacturing.
* Experience with NDE, including ultrasonic testing, dye penetrant, xray and others.
* Prior work transitioning propulsion assemblies from development to production environments with increasing build rate
* Familiarity with hazardous materials handling and safety protocols associated with propellant loading and propulsion acceptance testing

Pay Range
 
 

* Salary Range: $181,913 - $262,763/per year
* This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
* Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
* You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements
 
 
Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.
 
 
“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).
 
 
E-Verify Statement
 
 
Varda Space Industries, Inc. participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.
 
 
E-Verify Notice Right To Work Notice

Varda Space Industries is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, martial status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

records.title: Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Payloads)
records.description:
**About Varda**
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
**Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.**
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
 
 
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
 
 
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
 
 
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
 
 
**About This Role**
As the
**Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Payloads)**
at Varda, you will own the manufacturing and integration processes for the mission-critical payload systems that define what Varda's reentry capsules actually do in space. Varda's payloads — including pharmaceutical processing hardware, microgravity experiment modules, and government and commercial customer systems — represent the core value proposition of every mission. You will translate payload design requirements into production-ready assembly processes, develop rigorous work instructions, and work hands-on with technicians to ensure payloads are built, integrated, and verified to the highest standards of quality and cleanliness. This role demands both technical breadth and meticulous process discipline: you will interface with external payload customers, internal design teams, and the vehicle integration team to ensure every payload is ready to fly. If you are driven by the idea that what you manufacture will directly enable life-saving pharmaceuticals or cutting-edge scientific research in microgravity, this role is for you.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Own end-to-end manufacturing and assembly processes for Varda payload systems, including pharmaceutical processing hardware, experiment modules, and customer-furnished payload equipment
* Develop and maintain detailed work instructions, assembly travelers, process specifications, and acceptance test procedures for payload fabrication and integration operations
* Serve as the primary manufacturing interface for payload customers, translating customer requirements and ICD (Interface Control Document) constraints into executable production processes
* Implement contamination control, cleanliness, and handling protocols appropriate for sensitive payload hardware, including pharmaceutical-grade and precision optical components
* Collaborate with payload design engineers to provide DFM and DFA feedback on assembly accessibility, connector placement, thermal interface design, and testability
* Define and execute payload acceptance testing, functional verification checkouts, and pre-integration inspections; maintain complete and traceable build records
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for payload non-conformances; coordinate MRB dispositions with design engineering and, where applicable, payload customers
* Coordinate payload integration milestones with the vehicle integration team, ensuring payload readiness gates align with overall vehicle build schedule

**Basic Qualifications**

* B.S. in Mechanical, Biomedical Engineering, or a related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience (typically 6–10+ years)
* 6+ years of experience manufacturing or integrating complex and compact electromechanical assemblies, scientific instruments, or payload systems in aerospace, defense, biomedical, or research environments
* Demonstrated experience building and integrating precision hardware to tight tolerances and exacting cleanliness requirements
* Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, ICDs, and assembly models; familiarity with GD&T and interface requirement management
* Experience developing and executing assembly procedures and acceptance test plans for multi-functional hardware assemblies
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable interfacing directly with customers and cross-functional internal teams
* Must be physically able to regularly lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, and stand for extended periods while working directly with flight hardware

**Preferred Skills And Experience**

* M.S. degree in Mechanical engineering specialized in Fluid Mechanics, Biomedical Engineering, or related discipline
* Experience manufacturing or integrating spacecraft payloads, scientific instruments, or hosted payload modules for LEO, GEO, or deep space missions
* Familiarity with pharmaceutical or bioprocessing hardware manufacturing requirements, including GMP considerations and contamination control protocols relevant to in-space drug manufacturing
* Background managing payload customer relationships from hardware delivery through integration, verification, and launch readiness
* Experience with ICD management and interface verification processes for payload-to-spacecraft integration
* Knowledge of microgravity experiment hardware design considerations and their manufacturing implications
* Familiarity with environmental testing (thermal vacuum, vibration, shock) as it applies to payload hardware acceptance and qualification
* Experience working in or adjacent to a cleanroom environment (ISO Class 7 or better) for integration of sensitive flight payloads
* Prior work at a company developing commercial space services with a direct end-user product — pharmaceutical, government, or research — where manufacturing quality directly impacted mission outcome

Pay Range
 
 

* Salary Range: $181,913 - $262,763/per year
* This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
* Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
* You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements
 
 
Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.
 
 
“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).
 
 
E-Verify Statement
 
 
Varda Space Industries, Inc. participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.

Read more Read more
 
 
Varda Space Industries is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, martial status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

postedPay.title: Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch

records.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.
 
 
With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.
 
 
**LOCATION:**
Remote with Travel
 
 
US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.
 
 
This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.
 
 
The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**Key Performance Metrics**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**Qualifications**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**Education And/Or Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**Physical Demands**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

records.title: Director, New Product Development Engineering
records.description:
Bevi is on a mission to transform how beverages are delivered and consumed. Our connected beverage platform eliminates the need for single-use bottles and cans, making it easy, fun, and sustainable to stay hydrated. As the category leader in IoT-enabled beverage technology, we're building a future where Bevi machines are everywhere people live, work, and connect. We've raised over $160M in venture capital, serve thousands of customers across the US, Canada, UK and Ireland, and we've been rapidly growing year over year, saving over 1 billion bottles from waste. In addition to driving hypergrowth with our current product line, Bevi is heavily investing in new product development.
 
 
Bevi is hiring a Director of New Product Development Engineering to lead the team that designs our next generation of beverage machines and takes them into high-volume production. The work spans new platforms, smaller form-factor machines, hot water, flavor cartridges, and consumables, and brings together hardware, software, and beverage science.
 
 
Your top priority is scaling. You'll take Bevi's hardware into much higher-volume, lower-cost manufacturing, working closely with ODM, JDM, and overseas contract manufacturing partners. You'll lead NPD Engineering, Systems Engineering, and Compliance Engineering, and own new products from concept through certification and production launch.
 
 
This role reports to the VP of Engineering, sits on the engineering leadership team, and works across Product, Software, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, and more. Bevi is still growing fast, so you'll have real room to shape how we build hardware and the team that does it. Expect regular travel to manufacturing partners in Asia.
 
 
What You'll Own
 
 
New Product Development
 
 

* Lead new product programs from concept and prototype through EVT, DVT, PVT, and mass production.
* Own product architecture and make the tradeoff calls on cost, reliability, manufacturability, and schedule, while staying hands-on in design reviews and critical build issues.
* Set cost targets (BOM, tooling, landed cost) early and design to them, with DFM, DFA, and design-for-cost built in from the start.

High-Volume Manufacturing & Working with ODMs
 
 

* Lead Bevi's shift to high-volume, lower-cost manufacturing with ODM, JDM, and overseas contract manufacturing partners.
* Work with partner engineering teams as true collaborators: align on specs, work through design feedback together, and decide where their expertise can speed up our programs.
* Drive NPI and transfer to production, including pilot builds, line validation, and yield ramp, with time on-site during critical builds.

Systems Engineering & Compliance
 
 

* Guide Systems Engineering on requirements, architecture, DFMEA, and design verification across mechanical, electrical, firmware, software, and beverage subsystems.
* Oversee product safety and regulatory certification (UL, NSF, FCC, CE/UKCA, and food-contact requirements) so it supports international growth and stays off the critical path.

Team Leadership & Process
 
 

* Lead and grow a team of NPD, Systems, and Compliance engineers, including managers, aligned to one product roadmap.
* Recruit and develop engineering talent to build an organization that scales with Bevi's product strategy.
* Run a clear product development process, with phase gates and design reviews, that works for both in-house and partner-led programs.
* Champion the use of AI across the team to speed up design, analysis, testing, and documentation.

What We're Looking For
 
 

* 12+ years in hardware product development, including 5+ years leading multi-disciplinary engineering teams that include managers.
* Ability to be in the office 3+ days per week.
* Ability to travel up to 25%, including extended trips to overseas manufacturing partners.
* A track record of scaling electromechanical products into high-volume production (tens of thousands of units or more), ideally in consumer electronics, appliances, or connected devices.
* Hands-on experience partnering with ODMs and overseas contract manufacturers (Asia strongly preferred), from spec through design iterations, NPI, tooling, and yield ramp, including time on the ground with them.
* Strong design-for-cost and DFM/DFA skills, with a record of driving down BOM and landed cost at volume.
* Knowledge of high-volume manufacturing processes such as injection molding, sheet metal, die casting, and automated assembly.
* Experience with systems engineering practices and bringing products through safety and regulatory certification.
* A practical, hands-on approach to using AI tools in engineering work.
* A strong communicator who is credible in a design review, on a factory floor, and in a leadership meeting.
* BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field. Experience with fluid, thermal, or food and beverage systems is a plus.

At Bevi, We Believe Compensation Is a Powerful Tool To Attract, Retain, And Grow Talent. Our Compensation Philosophy Centers On 5 Principles
 
 

* Market-driven - We anchor pay decisions in real-time market data
* Performance-based - We reward individual impact, not just tenure
* Equitable - We ensure fairness across teams, roles, and demographics
* Growth-focused - We invest in talent that scales with Bevi
* Total Rewards approach - We strategically balance base pay, bonuses, benefits, and equity

The posted compensation range reflects the salary\* for this position. Some roles may be eligible for a commission plan or a bonus incentive. All Bevi employees receive equity in the form of stock options. All full-time employees are invited to participate in our Total Rewards plan, which includes health & medical benefits, flexible spending accounts, flexible PTO, and more. Offers to join Bevi are based on a few criteria, including the scope of the role, the candidate's work experience, targeted skills, internal equity of the team, and external market data.
 
 

* For Sales roles: The posted range reflects base salary plus commission which is the total potential on target earnings (OTE) for the position.

Pay Range
 
 
$195,840—$230,400 USD
 
 
**Benefits**

* Comprehensive medical, dental and vision insurance plans with BlueCross BlueShield, 95% paid by employer
* 401(k) with company match
* Flexible PTO plus 12 company holidays, and additional paid days for sick leave, etc
* Generous fully paid parental leave for both birth parents and non-birth parents
* Fully employer paid disability and life insurances
* Wellness and fitness reimbursements
* Monthly stipends for cell phone use and commuting costs
* Onsite snacks, weekly catered lunch, and (of course) unlimited Bevi ... plus composting and terra-cycling, too
* Happy hours, team-building events, bagel breakfasts, Values awards - and more.

**A note on AI in our hiring process**
: We use AI to help synthesize interview notes and surface themes from feedback, keeping our process consistent as we grow. Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and interviews may be recorded to support note-taking, just let us know if you'd prefer we don't. We'll also ask how you're learning and experimenting with AI in your work. Growing our AI fluency is something every Bevi team member is committed to and invested in.
 
 
Our commitment to responsible innovation is reflected in our partnership with the Mass AI Coalition, a collaboration that aligns with our dedication to community-driven progress and the future of technology.
 
 
*We're passionate about supporting career growth and would love to be part of your professional journey. We also know that talent comes in many forms. We value individual accomplishments, specialized knowledge, and genuine passion over simply checking boxes on a requirements list. Whether you're a seasoned expert or an emerging talent, we're looking for people who are ready to build what's next. If any of our open positions interest you, we'd encourage you to apply!*
*A member of the Bevi Talent team 'recruiting@bevi.co' will be reaching out about next steps if we would like to move forward.*
**Accommodations**
Bevi is committed to an inclusive hiring process and we aim to provide accommodations for persons with disabilities. If you need any accommodations for the application or throughout the interview process please contact recruiting@bevi.co.
