records.description:
**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
 
 
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
This position is incentive eligible.
 
 
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/
 
 
**POSTING TIMELINE**
The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.
 
 
Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At
**Honeywell Aerospace**
(NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.
 
 
Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.
 
 
Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.
 
 
Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.
 
 
Honeywell Aerospace Products And Services Are Found On Aircraft Across Commercial Aviation, Defense And Space. We Operate Through Three Business Areas
 
 
Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft
 
 
Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying
 
 
Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board
 
 
With approximately 58,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, we are also advancing systems for autonomous and supersonic platforms — bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. Explore our businesses: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com
 
 
Join Honeywell Aerospace! Our aerospace innovations bring people together, make the world safer and more secure, and help humankind reach for the stars. Now we’re shaping aviation’s future with sustainable aviation fuels, smarter cockpits, ultra-efficient engines, smart airports, flying taxis and much more.

postedPay.title: Senior Manager, Pixel Buds Product Operations

records.description:
**Minimum qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 10 years of experience managing hardware new product introduction (NPI) processes, factory ramp, and consumer electronics manufacturing operations.
* Experience leading and managing cross-functional technical teams (e.g., Operations Program Managers, Technical Program Managers, Supply Chain Program Managers).
* Experience partnering with external original design manufacturers (ODMs) and electronics manufacturing services (EMS) partners through Ok2Ship.

**Preferred qualifications:**

* Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience delivering high-volume audio, wearables, or miniaturized consumer electronics hardware products.
* Experience driving Design for Manufacturability (DFM) and Design for Cost (DFC) initiatives across international agreement manufacturing sites.
* Experience managing engineering operations programs with executive-level stakeholder reporting and cross-functional hardware lifecycle alignment.

**About The Job**
A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Program Manager at Google, you’ll lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish — working with stakeholders to plan requirements, manage project schedules, identify risks, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. Your projects will often span offices, time zones, and hemispheres. It's your job to coordinate the players and keep them up to date on progress and deadlines.
 
 
The Head of Pixel Product Operations (Buds) will be responsible for the development and launch of Pixel Buds through the New Product Introduction (NPI) process through Ok2Ship, across the portfolio of Pixel Buds. You will be responsible for identifying and evolving best practices, and sustaining an organization that has scaled with execution.
 
 
You will lead a global team of various manufacturing teams - Operations Program Managers, System Technical Program Managers, Mechanical Technical Program Managers and Supply Chain Program Managers directly. As the Primary Manager from the Global Operations and Supply Chain organization responsible for the launch of the Pixel Buds programs, several other cross-functional teams rely on your leadership to guide the programs and products to success. You will need to balance engineering, operations, and quality processes and take into account the competitive dynamics to surpass the rate of innovation in the consumer electronics industry. This will encompass supporting large volume products and first generation products within the Pixel portfolio.
 
 
Google's mission is to organize the world's information and make it universally accessible and useful. Our Devices & Services team combines the best of Google AI, Software, and Hardware to create radically helpful experiences for users. We research, design, and develop new technologies and hardware to make our user's interaction with computing faster, seamless, and more powerful. Whether finding new ways to capture and sense the world around us, advancing form factors, or improving interaction methods, the Devices & Services team is making people's lives better through technology.
 
 
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
 
 
US: $236000 - $329000 (USD) + 25% bonus target + equity + benefits
 
 
**Responsibilities**
Learn more about benefits at Google .
 
 

* Design, execute, and implement end-to-end factory and manufacturing solutions and processes and associated strategies that take into account the engaged dynamics of the Google hardware business.
* Lead a team of Operations professionals across both technical and non-technical domains to drive rapid time to market at immediate scale, with no compromise to Product Quality..
* Direct cross-functional teams across other business functions and initiatives in close partnership with key stakeholder groups like Hardware Engineering, Supplier Development Engineering, Software Engineering, Sourcing and Procurement, and Logistics.
* Create a culture that balances agility and flexibility with the expectation of new products that can scale.

Google is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. See also Google's EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing our Accommodations for Applicants form .

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.
 
 
Collins Aerospace is a leader in technologically advanced, intelligent solutions that help redefine the aerospace and defense industry. With a comprehensive portfolio and deep technical expertise, we help customers meet the demands of the global market. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.
 
 
The OPM & NPI Lead serves as the primary operational leader responsible for the successful execution of both sustaining programs and New Product Introduction (NPI) initiatives. This role provides leadership for a team of Operations Product Managers while ensuring operational readiness, production launch success, customer commitment attainment, and portfolio performance. Acting as the operational integrator between General Management, Program Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, and SIOP functions, the OPM & NPI Lead drives execution across the entire product lifecycle. The role ensures new products transition effectively from development into production while maintaining delivery, cost, quality, inventory, and capacity objectives for existing programs.
 
 
Must be willing and able to travel 15% of the time.
 
 
**What You Will Do:**
*Portfolio Leadership*

* Provide operations leadership within Program Management Teams
* Lead and develop a team of Operations Product Managers
* Establish priorities and allocate resources across product portfolios
* Ensure alignment of customer commitments with manufacturing capacity
* Lead portfolio reviews and executive status reporting
* Support business growth initiatives and strategic program execution
* Develop business cases supporting investments and growth opportunities

*New Product Introduction (NPI)*

* Lead operational execution of NPI programs from concept through production stabilization
* Conduct manufacturing feasibility and producibility assessments
* Ensure readiness of labor, equipment, tooling, facilities, materials, and processes
* Lead launch readiness reviews and milestone assessments
* Manage transition from development to recurring production
* Manufacturing Operations Leadership
* Translate forecasted demand into executable manufacturing plans
* Lead recovery efforts for missed deliveries and production disruptions
* Develop capacity models and identify future resource requirements
* Manage operational risks and mitigation strategies

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Typically requires a University Degree and minimum 10 years prior relevant experience or an Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 7 years of experience
* 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing, operations, program management, or NPI leadership
* 5+ years of leadership experience with direct reports
* Experience leading cross-functional teams in a complex manufacturing environment
* 3+ years experience managing new product introductions and production transitions
* Understanding of SIOP, capacity planning, production control, and operational performance metrics

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Business, or related discipline
* Aerospace or defense manufacturing experience
* Electron Beam Welding (EBW)
* Electro Chemical Machining (ECM)
* Precision machining and assembly operations
* Special process manufacturing
* AS9100 and NADCAP experience
* Lean Manufacturing, CORE, Six Sigma, or PMP certification
* Experience with SAP, MES/Solumina, Pelico, Power BI, Tableau, and advanced planning systems
* Experience leading operational recovery and turnaround initiatives

**What We Offer:**
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
 
 
**Some of our competitive benefits package includes:**

* Three weeks of vacation for newly hired employees
* Generous 401(k) plan that includes employer matching funds and separate employer retirement contribution, including a Lifetime Income Strategy option
* Tuition program
* Student Loan Repayment Program
* Life insurance and disability coverage
* Optional coverages you can buy pet insurance, home and auto insurance, additional life and accident insurance, critical illness insurance, group legal, ID theft protection
* Birth, adoption, parental leave benefits
* Ovia Health, fertility, andreimbursement family planning
* Adoption Assistance
* Autism Benefit
* Employee Assistance Plan, including up to 10 free counseling sessions
* Healthy You Incentives, wellness rewards program
* Doctor on Demand, virtual doctor visits
* Bright Horizons, child and elder care services
* Teladoc Medical Experts, second opinion program
* And more!

**Learn More and Apply Now:**
**Onsite:**
Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products.
 
 
The next chapter of our future as an aerospace company is here, and we are excited about what this means for our employees and customers! Get onboard the Collins Aerospace Operations team and play a part in managing our innovative products from inception to delivery. The Operations team continues to grow and aims to strengthen the connection of Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain and Environment, Health & Safety (EH&S) across Collins Aerospace. In this dynamic environment, you will have the opportunity to network across our businesses and functions, all while improving the productivity, quality and efficiency of our operations worldwide.
 
 
At Collins, the paths we pave together lead to limitless possibility. And the bonds we form – with our customers and with each other -- propel us all higher, again and again. Apply now and be part of the team that’s redefining aerospace, every day.
 
 
***As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote.***
The salary range for this role is 132,400 USD - 251,600 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills.
 
 
Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement.
 
 
Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance.
 
 
This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply.
 
 
RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window.
 
 
*RTX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected class. RTX provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with a Disability and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.*

records.title: Senior Manager, Product Development & Production
records.description:
Studs is a category-defining ear piercing and earring brand named one of "the 10 most innovative companies in retail for 2023" by Fast Company. Studs connects ear piercing with aftercare and earring shopping to create an end-to-end Earscaping® experience. We offer a better retail and digital experience that prioritizes safety and expertise in a cool, fun and welcoming environment, along with a wide earring assortment—all at an accessible price point.
 
 
The Senior Manager of Product Development & Production is responsible for execution of proposed product and design. They will take the product from the proposed design state to commercialization including physical product development and final production. They will also be responsible for building out a team org structure and training new team members
 
 
**Salary Range:**
$130,000
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:**
Product Development
 
 

* Establish strategic partnerships with suppliers, manufacturers, and other vendors in order to develop new products or improve existing products
* Oversee the product life cycle of new products from concept to commercialization
* Develop and manage the development calendar with milestones that aligns with the organization's strategic objective
* Manage all vendor WIPs, sample requests and inbound samples
* Price negotiation to achieve margin goals
* Work with external partners on brand collaboration products and key initiatives

Production
 
 

* Oversee production process from PO placement through ex-factory including vendor payment and credits
* Ensure bulk goods produced conform with approved designs and standards
* Set factory allocation to ensure they align with factories' capacity supporting the businesses growth and key initiatives
* Negotiate bulk inventory costs, lead times and deliveries
* Manage and resolve any manufacturing issues including delivery delays with factories
* Communicate delivery timelines and collaborate with cross functional partners on product launches

Testing & Relations
 
 

* Foster and maintain vendor relationships
* Lead on boarding process ensuring factory and vendor adherence to Stud's processes and standards, and that clear understanding of processes and nuances between vendors is maintained
* Develop and monitor, and continually improve quality assurance procedures and processes with external testing vendors
* Ensure all products manufactured that will be commercially sold are tested to STUDS standards prior to shipment
* Evaluate, improve, and define processes and policies, process implementation, and identify errors and areas of improvement
* Address the root causes of quality issues, create corrective action plans and implement long term solutions in partnership with external vendors

**Requirements:**

* 5+ years of experience in product development and/or production, with hands-on ownership of products from concept through bulk delivery.
* Jewelry experience strongly preferred, but not required. Experience in accessories or another consumer product category is a plus.
* Retail or DTC brand experience a plus, especially in a multi-channel business (physical retail and ecommerce).
* 2+ years of people management experience, or a demonstrated record of training and developing team members. Interest in building a team structure from the ground up.
* Proven track record managing overseas and domestic factory partners, including vendor onboarding, factory allocation, and capacity planning.
* Highly organized, with the ability to run a development calendar across many SKUs, vendors, and launches at once in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
* Clear, direct communicator who works well across functions, including Merchandising, Finance, Retail, and Marketing.
* Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills. AI fluency preferred: comfortable using AI tools in daily work to move faster.
* Based in New York, NY and able to work from the HQ office on a hybrid schedule.
* Driven, creative problem solver that consistently acts with integrity and speaks up
* Owner's mindset, with the ability to approach feedback and problems with a positive attitude.

**Benefits & Perks**

* Flexible Work Environment (3 days in office, 2 days work from home)
* Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (including a plan option with $0 in-network mental health visits)
* Access to Mental Health and Work/Life Resources including Online Therapy, Gender Affirmation Support Services, and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Voluntary Life Insurance
* Health and Commuter Tax-Advantaged Accounts
* Stock Options in connection with the Company's Equity Incentive Plan
* 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan
* Paid Time Off, Paid Safe & Sick Leave, and Paid Parental Leave
* Paid Sabbatical After 4 Years of Service
* Exclusive Employee Discounts on Piercings and Jewelry (we've got your friends and family covered too!)
* Access to PerkSpot and additional benefits such as pet insurance, discounted tickets, personal finance coaching, healthy rewards, and more!

*Studs is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing a work environment that fosters diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunity without regard to race, color, gender, age, creed, sex, religion, national origin, disability (physical or mental), marital status, citizenship, ancestry, sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression, or any other legally protected status. Studs considers qualified applicants with criminal histories. We comply with applicable state and local laws prohibiting discrimination in employment in every jurisdiction in which we operate. If you require an accommodation for the application process, please email HRBP@studs.com.*
*Massachusetts Applicants: It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.*
*Click here for the Studs Privacy Notice for California Applicants.*

records.company: Granite State Manufacturing - Allard Nazarian Group
records.title: Director of Quality
records.description:
Granite State Manufacturing is a leading contract manufacturer of large, complex, precision machined and welded components, supporting the US Navy in building submarines.

We specialize in high-mix, low-to-medium volume production, delivering precision, quality, and on-time performance on custom-engineered products. Our capabilities include:

* Large-format CNC machining
* Heavy fabrication and welding (MIG, TIG, FCAW, SAW)
* Assembly, inspection, and testing
* Program management for complex builds

We are known for handling tight tolerances, complex geometries, and demanding customer specifications.

Our work environment is supportive, providing what our people need to do great work.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

Plans, coordinates, and directs quality program designed to ensure continuous production of products consistent with established standards. Continuously increasing Quality Awareness across the company, with the goal of reducing and eliminating barriers and obstacles to throughput, while reducing overall cost and schedule. Leadership, both within the QC/QA staff, and across all departments, is expected to make it easier for employees to make quality products, and make it easier for customers to do business with GSM.

We strive to make things faster, better, and less expensively.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* You will be the face of Quality to our customers, and will participate in program reviews with GSM and Customer senior management.
* Leading our Continuous Improvement efforts will provide you with the ability to make substantial changes to our internal processes and procedures across the board, in our constant efforts to be more efficient, more effective, and more valuable to our customers.
* Directs workers engaged in inspection and testing activities to ensure continuous control over materials, facilities, and products.
* In addition to the Quality Engineers and Quality Assurance Specialists, your direct reports will include the Quality Inspectors and Quality Administrators. Working closely together with your team you will make great use of complementary skills and experience, and be most effective in bringing GSM‘s performance to the next
* Plans, promotes, and organizes training activities related to product quality and reliability.
* Be the face of Quality to customers and participate in program reviews with GSM and customer senior management.
* Build a path with continuous improvement efforts to be more efficient, more effective, and more valuable to customers. Strive to increase production speed, improve quality, and reduce
* Participates in evaluation of Vendor Quality.
* Demonstrates responsibility and accountability for creating a professional, safe, and clean environment evidenced by: being at work on time to perform assigned duties, following the policies of Granite State Manufacturing, always wearing safety glasses in designated areas, maintaining a neat and orderly work area, and following safety practices to prevent errors.
* Demonstrates commitment to teamwork by establishing effective relationships and networks with both managers/directors and workers, and collaborating with them to accomplish shared purposes and goals.
* Abides by GSM Code of Ethics and Business Conduct standards and strictly observes all U.S. and foreign laws and regulations.

**EEO STATEMENT**

Granite State Manufacturing (GSM) is an equal opportunity employer. GSM does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, national origin, citizenship, veteran status, age, physical or mental disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state, or local laws in its programs, activities, or employment.

 **Requirements**

**QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**

* **Bachelor's degree and related experience and /or training or equivalent combination of education and experience.**
* Knowledge of manufacturing methods, product design, metallurgy, customer requirements, military specification, NDT and documentation systems.
* **Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.**
* **Experience in defense/aerospace related job fabrication and welding environment**
* **Experience with manufacturing processes to include: CNC machining, painting, Fabrication techniques and weld processes in a heavily regulated environment such as DOD or Aerospace**
* **Ability to write technical reports, ISO procedures and correspondence.**
* **Ability to deal with difficult problems involving ambiguous circumstances in non-standardized situations.**

 
**Benefits**

**BENEFITS**

Compensation & Benefits

* Competitive salary
* Medical insurance
* Dental & Vision, Life insurance (Company paid)
* Disability benefits (Company paid)
* 401(k) & 401(k) company matching
* Paid time off and holidays
* Flexible spending accounts
* Health savings account
* Referral program
* Overtime opportunities (if applicable)
* Training and career growth in advanced manufacturing
* Employee assistance program

Why Join Us?

* Work on large-scale, one-of-a-kind projects
* Stable industry with strong customer demand
* Opportunity to grow in a flexible, high-skill environment

records.title: Director, Risk Management and Quality
records.description:
**Director of Risk Management and Quality**

**Who We Are:**

At Triangle Springs, we are committed to empowering and supporting a diverse and determined workforce who can drive quality, scalability, and significant impact across our hospitals and communities. In your role, you’ll support those that are in our facilities who are interfacing and providing care to our patients and community members. We believe that our collective efforts will shape a healthier future for the communities we serve. Our programs offer customized rehabilitation tailored to the specific needs of those recovering from a stroke, brain injury, neurological conditions, trauma, spinal cord injury, amputation or orthopedic injury.

**Why Choose Us:**

* Affordable medical, dental and vision plans provided to meet the needs of full-time employees and their families
* Competitive Paid Time Off
* Tuition reimbursement, continuing education opportunities and apprenticeship programs for eligible employees
* 401(K) retirement plans
* Flexible spending and health savings accounts

**How you’ll contribute:**

The Director of Risk Management and Quality is responsible for the development and administration of Performance Improvement, Risk Management, and Staff Development activities throughout the hospital to ensure that all state, federal, and Joint Commission standards for care are consistently met. The Director collects and analyzes data on hospital performance, incidents, and documentation to improve hospital performance and ensure provision of quality care. The Director works closely with all department leaders to recommend and provide required staff development and tailored programs based upon data analysis. The Director monitors, investigates, and as required, reports all hospital incidents. 
 
**Essential Functions:**

To perform this job, an individual must perform each essential function satisfactorily with or without reasonable accommodation.

* Provides oversight and continuous monitoring of the hospital’s quality program, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and best‑practice standards.
* Demonstrates comprehensive expertise in all applicable regulatory requirements, including The Joint Commission (TJC), Medicaid, and state and federal healthcare laws.
* Serves as a key advisor to department leaders by interpreting regulatory standards, offering guidance, and supporting compliance readiness.
* Partners with hospital staff to proactively identify risk and safety concerns, leading the development and execution of corrective action plans.
* Collects, analyzes, and interprets performance data to evaluate hospital outcomes and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Oversees the incident reporting process, ensuring timely documentation, investigation, data analysis, and reporting to the Quality Council and the Chief Executive Officer.
* Utilizes the Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act (PDCA) methodology to design, implement, and measure improvement initiatives that enhance quality and patient safety.
* Ensures ongoing organizational compliance with all regulatory standards and applicable laws, maintaining survey readiness at all times.
* Always exhibit the company’s core values of champion patient care, do the right thing, embrace individuality, act with kindness, and making a difference together.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in counseling, Social Work, Nursing, or related clinical field from an accredited school required. Master’s degree in clinical field from an accredited school preferred.
* Counseling, Social Work, or Registered Nurse license preferred.
* Three years of risk management and regulatory compliance in a healthcare setting are required.
* CPR certification is required within 30 days of employment and prior to any patient contact.
* De-escalation certification is required within 30 days of employment and prior to any patient contact.

**EEOC Statement:**

Triangle Springs is committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunities for all applicants and employees and complies with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination against any employee or applicant for employment because of color, race, sex, age, religion, national origin, disability, genetic information, gender identity, sexual orientation, veterans' status or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

We employ and provide care to people from all walks of life. We are committed to promoting healing, providing hope, preserving dignity and producing value with an inclusive workforce in which diversity is leveraged, respected, and reflective of the patients, family members, customers and team members we serve.Lifepoint Health is a leader in community-based care and driven by a mission of Making Communities Healthier. Our diversified healthcare delivery network spans 29 states and includes 63 community hospital campuses, 32 rehabilitation and behavioral health hospitals, and more than 170 additional sites of care across the healthcare continuum, such as acute rehabilitation units, outpatient centers and post-acute care facilities. We believe that success is achieved through talented people. We want to create places where employees want to work, with opportunities to pursue meaningful and satisfying careers that truly make a difference in communities across the country.

records.title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine

postedPay.title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine

records.description:
Department Overview:

The Department of Medicine (DoM) at OHSU is comprised of a diverse community of faculty, staff, clinicians, researchers, educators, and learners dedicated to advancing patient care, education, and research across ten divisions.

The Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, quality management, and performance improvement support for inpatient clinical services across the Department of Medicine's ten specialty divisions and care sites. Reporting to the Vice Chair of Clinical Practice and partnering closely with the Vice Chair for Administration, this position serves as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and clinical effectiveness initiatives.

Function/Duties of Position:

Working collaboratively with DoM and OHSU Health quality leaders, division leadership, hospital operations, finance, revenue cycle, informatics, care management, nursing leadership, clinical documentation teams, and physician leaders, the Director advances the Department's inpatient quality, operational, clinical, and financial goals through the design, implementation, and oversight of standardized processes, performance improvement efforts, operational reporting, and strategic initiatives.

Emphasis is placed on quality programing and outcomes, patient safety, clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, revenue cycle performance, operational efficiency, provider productivity, inpatient capacity management, and growth planning across all Department of Medicine inpatient services. The Director supports a broad portfolio of inpatient programs spanning multiple clinical specialties and care settings.

This position functions within a highly matrixed environment and serves as a key liaison between departmental leadership and enterprise partners, ensuring alignment with OHSU Health strategic priorities, quality objectives, and high-reliability organizational principles.

**Inpatient Quality and Operations Leadership and Oversight**

* Work in direct partnership with the DoM Vice Chair of Clinical Practice, DoM Associate Vice Chair of Inpatient Services, Healthcare quality leaders, and other institutional leaders to oversee and coordinate quality-focused inpatient care across Department of Medicine divisions.
* Provide strategic administrative leadership and operational oversight for Department of Medicine inpatient programs and services.
* Serve as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and performance improvement initiatives.
* Partner with division heads, section heads, medical directors, healthcare administrators, quality leaders, and physician leaders to identify and address operational and quality barriers affecting patient safety, access, efficiency, provider experience, and clinical outcomes.
* Shape and implement standardized inpatient quality, safety, and operational best practices across medicine specialties.
* Coordinate departmental quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing medical errors, serious safety events, healthcare-associated infections, hospital-acquired conditions, avoidable readmissions, preventable complications, and patient harm.
* Lead administrative efforts related to inpatient quality programs, patient safety activities, inpatient capacity management, patient flow, consult services, discharge efficiency, care coordination, and service-line optimization.
* Support departmental participation in mortality reviews, safety event reviews, quality committees, accreditation activities, regulatory preparedness efforts, and institutional quality initiatives.
* Establish and maintain departmental quality and operational governance structures, including scorecards, dashboards, performance reviews, and accountability processes.
* Partner with healthcare quality teams to identify opportunities for improvement and coordinate development of corrective action plans.
* Serve as the primary administrative liaison between Department of Medicine leadership, inpatient programs, Healthcare quality teams, and hospital operations leadership.
* Monitor operational, quality, and patient safety performance measures and drive action planning to improve outcomes.
* Facilitate multidisciplinary teams and stakeholder groups responsible for advancing inpatient quality, safety, throughput, and operational effectiveness.

**Revenue Cycle, Billing, Coding, and Clinical Documentation Integrity**

* Serve as the Department's operational lead for inpatient professional revenue cycle performance.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Professional Coding, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI), Finance, Compliance, and physician leaders to improve revenue capture, reimbursement, and operational performance.
* Evaluate and improve inpatient provider documentation practices, coding accuracy, charge capture processes, and billing workflows.
* Lead provider education efforts related to documentation requirements, coding regulations, payer expectations, reimbursement methodologies, and compliance standards.
* Monitor inpatient professional fee performance, wRVU generation, Case Mix Index (CMI), coding trends, denials, reimbursement outcomes, and documentation quality measures.
* Develop dashboards and performance reporting tools that support transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Identify specialty-specific opportunities for revenue optimization, operational efficiency, and documentation improvement.

**Performance Improvement and Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead complex inpatient operational and quality improvement initiatives utilizing Lean, process improvement, project management, and change management methodologies.
* Design and implement department-wide initiatives focused on improving quality outcomes, patient safety, throughput, provider experience, financial performance, and operational consistency.
* Conduct workflow analyses and redesign efforts to eliminate inefficiencies, reduce variation in care delivery, and improve service performance.
* Collaborate with Quality, Analytics, Finance, Informatics, and Operations teams to establish measurable goals and monitor outcomes.
* Develop project charters, implementation plans, success metrics, and performance benchmarks for strategic initiatives.
* Support departmental strategic planning activities and implementation of enterprise priorities related to inpatient growth, quality, and operational excellence.
* Advance high-reliability organization principles and support compliance with accreditation and regulatory requirements.

**Data Analytics, Reporting, and Financial Performance**

* Develop and maintain operational, financial, quality, patient safety, and utilization reporting structures for departmental and divisional leadership.
* Establish and maintain comprehensive inpatient quality scorecards and dashboards.
* Monitor and analyze key performance indicators including:
 + Analyze trends in inpatient volumes, utilization, consult activity, throughput, revenue cycle performance, patient outcomes, and quality metrics.
 + Translate complex operational and quality data into actionable recommendations for leaders.
 + Benchmark Department performance against institutional, regional, and national metrics when available.
 + Support financial forecasting, business case development, and investment planning for inpatient growth initiatives.

**Stakeholder Engagement and Committee Leadership**

* Represent the Department of Medicine on institutional committees related to quality, patient safety, inpatient operations, revenue cycle, clinical documentation, care management, patient flow, and performance improvement.
* Build collaborative partnerships with hospital administrators, nursing leaders, physicians, quality teams, informatics, finance, and operational stakeholders.
* Provide subject matter expertise regarding inpatient quality, safety, operational performance, workflow redesign, and professional revenue optimization.
* Lead communication, stakeholder engagement, and change management activities for major inpatient initiatives.
* Support development of a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, patient safety, and operational excellence throughout Department of Medicine inpatient programs.

Required Qualifications:

**Education**

Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, finance, or a related field is required. Master’s degree may substitute for one (1) year of experience.

**Experience**

* Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in clinical operations or healthcare administration, with at least two (2) years in a formal leadership role.
* Experience supporting inpatient hospital operations, quality improvement, patient safety, healthcare finance, revenue cycle, or operational excellence initiatives.
* Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives within healthcare organizations.
* Experience working collaboratively with physician leaders, nursing leadership, and hospital operational teams.
* Experience developing performance metrics, scorecards, dashboards, and operational improvement plans.

**Competencies**

* Strong knowledge of inpatient healthcare operations and physician practice management.
* Strong knowledge of healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, performance measurement, and high-reliability organizational principles.
* Knowledge of inpatient reimbursement methodologies, documentation requirements, clinical coding, and revenue cycle practices.
* Knowledge of regulatory, accreditation, and quality reporting requirements affecting inpatient healthcare delivery.
* Advanced analytical, reporting, and data interpretation skills.
* Demonstrated ability to develop quality scorecards, operational dashboards, and executive-level performance reporting.
* Ability to analyze complex clinical, operational, financial, and quality data and translate findings into actionable improvement strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to manage large-scale operational and performance improvement initiatives across multiple clinical specialties.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary efforts focused on reducing medical errors, improving patient outcomes, and advancing a culture of safety.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
* Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes without direct authority.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, Epic, reporting platforms, and healthcare analytics tools.
* Strong financial acumen, strategic planning, and business case development capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications:

**Education**

Master’s Degree in Health Care Administration, Business, Public Health or Nursing; or Bachelor’s degree with equivalent combination of education, experience and training.

**Experience**

* Eight or more years of progressively responsible healthcare operations, quality, or performance improvement experience.
* Academic medical center experience.
* Experience with inpatient physician billing and professional fee revenue cycle.
* Experience with quality reporting, patient safety programs, accreditation activities, and regulatory readiness.
* Experience with Epic reporting, provider productivity analysis, CDI initiatives, and coding optimization.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement certification or training.
* Matrix leadership experience.

**Competencies**

Demonstrated ability to leverage advanced analytics, financial modeling, forecasting tools, artificial intelligence-enabled technologies, and other data-driven methodologies to improve operational efficiency, inform strategic decision-making, optimize resource allocation, and support sustainable program growth.

Additional Details:

Professional office environment; may include occasional travel to affiliate and partner sites. In-person work schedule expected, with limited telework acceptable.

Operates in an environment with frequent interruptions, multiple competing priorities, and extensive interaction with faculty, staff, trainees, and institutional partners.

Physical location: Marquam Hill (primary)

Why apply to OHSU?: **We are Oregon's only public academic health center.** In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington. **All are welcome.** OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply. To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu

records.title: Director of Quality Assurance
records.description:
**Director of Quality Assurance** 
Location: 203A Log Canoe Circle, Stevensville, MD 21666 
Shift Hours: 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday through Friday 
Pay Range: $135,000 -175,000 + Bonus Eligibility!

**Hydrasearch,** a proud affiliate of The Dixon Group, is looking for a **Director of Quality Assurance** to join our team in **Stevensville, MD**! The Director of Quality Assurance will lead the organization's quality management strategy and ensure compliance with customer, industry, and regulatory requirements. This role is responsible for overseeing quality assurance programs, driving continuous improvement initiatives, managing quality personnel, and partnering with operations, engineering, and supply chain teams to maintain high standards of product quality and operational excellence.

**At Hydrasearch, we value the contributions of our Military Veterans and proudly employ our nation’s heroes. Veterans are strongly encouraged to apply.**

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead and manage the Quality Assurance function across the organization.
* Develop, implement, and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS).
* Ensure compliance with AS9100D and ISO 9001, customer requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Establish quality objectives, metrics, and reporting processes to drive continuous improvement.
* Oversee internal audits, external audits, and customer quality assessments.
* Manage corrective and preventive action (CAPA) programs and root cause analysis initiatives.
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Operations leadership to improve product and process quality.
* Analyze quality data and performance trends to identify improvement opportunities.
* Lead customer complaint investigations and resolution efforts.
* Develop and drive supplier quality programs. Actively work with vendors to address quality concerns.
* Build, mentor, and develop quality personnel and future leaders within the organization.
* Support new product introduction activities by ensuring quality standards are incorporated into design and manufacturing processes.
* Prepare and present quality performance updates to executive leadership.

**What We're Looking For:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, or a related technical field required; Master's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality leadership experience within manufacturing, maritime & aerospace defense, industrial, or related industries required; experience supporting defense, military, or government-contract manufacturing environments preferred.
* 5+ years of experience leading quality teams and managing direct reports.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100D & ISO 9001 quality systems.
* Experience leading internal and external audits.
* Demonstrated success implementing continuous improvement programs and driving measurable results.
* Experience with root cause analysis methodologies and corrective action processes.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and quality management tools.
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and statistical process control methodologies is a plus!
* This hands-on leadership position requires extensive maritime and aerospace defense quality experience, strong knowledge of industry standards and regulations, and proven success managing external audits and compliance initiatives.

**What We Offer:**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your family
* Competitive salary
* Bonus programs
* 401K retirement plan
* Training opportunities
* Tuition reimbursement
* Paid vacation, PTO, and holidays
* Gym reimbursements, and more!

**Who We Are:** Hydrasearch is a U.S. manufacturer specializing in fluid-transfer and control systems for maritime, aerospace, and defense applications. Since its founding in 1962, Hydrasearch has developed capabilities in hose assemblies, valve fittings, and customer machined parts, often to meet MIL-SPEC and naval standards.

**Join us and be a part of a team that values your contributions and supports your goals!**

**We do not provide sponsorships to work in the United States.**

###### **The Dixon Group is an equal opportunity employer. It is the Company's policy and practice to recruit, hire, train, and promote individuals, as well as to administer all personnel actions, compensation, and benefits, without regard to race, religion, color, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, ancestry or national origin, age, disability, family medical history or genetic information, veteran status, military service, or any other factors protected by applicable law. This policy extends to all employees and applicants and to all aspects of the employment relationship.**

###### **The Dixon Group is committed to protecting the privacy rights of its employees and job applicants to the fullest extent required by applicable law. To that end, personal information will be collected solely for those legitimate business purposes recognized by law, and then maintained in a manner consistent with all applicable laws and regulations pertaining to document retention requirements. The Dixon Group does not sell personal information to third parties, and does not share such personal information with third parties except when authorized by law to do so (e.g., in response to a lawful subpoena; mandatory tax reporting; etc.)**

Please contact us at (410) 778-2000 or hr@dixonvalve.com if you need help to participate fully in the application process.

Equal Opportunity Employer 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

records.description:
At Kailera, we are bold, authentic and committed to our mission of developing therapies that give people the power to transform their lives and elevate their overall health. Rooted in an entrepreneurial spirit and a team-oriented culture, we are working together to advance Kailera's mission to advance novel therapies for obesity and related conditions.
 
 
We are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes collaboration, integrity, and excellence. As we expand, we seek the most talented individuals with diverse backgrounds, cultures, perspectives, and experiences to join our team.

**What You'll Do:**

Kailera is preparing to bring its therapies to patients, and the Senior Director, GMP Quality Assurance will lead the quality strategy that gets us there. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance, you will be accountable for GMP Quality across drug substance, drug product, packaging/labeling, testing, stability, and product release as Kailera moves from late-stage clinical supply to commercial manufacturing and launch. You will develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy, build the quality systems and team needed for a compliant and reliable commercial supply chain, and serve as a trusted quality leader with Technical Operations, Regulatory, Supply Chain, and our network of contract manufacturers and testing laboratories.

 

*Required location: Waltham, MA (hub-based, onsite 3-4 days per week) OR Remote (home-based, onsite at a hub 1 week every other month).*

 

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy and roadmap, aligned with company and functional objectives, to support registration, launch, and lifecycle supply of Kailera products
* Be accountable for the performance and results of the GMP Quality function, including key quality initiatives, goals, and product assets
* Evolve the Kailera Quality Management System from clinical phase to commercial readiness, including change control, deviations/CAPA, complaints, product quality reviews, supplier management, training, and data integrity
* Define GMP quality metrics and KPIs for Quality Management Review, and use trends to anticipate risks and drive continuous improvement across the manufacturing network
* Advise senior leadership on quality risks, compliance trade-offs, and changes in the global regulatory environment, translating external trends into Kailera's quality strategy
* Lead the quality aspects of commercial readiness, including oversight of process performance qualification (PPQ), process and analytical method validation, commercial specifications, and stability programs
* Lead pre-approval and pre-license inspection (PAI/PLI) readiness across Kailera and contract manufacturing sites; host or support health authority inspections and drive timely, effective responses and commitments
* Partner with Regulatory CMC to ensure commercial manufacturing and controls are consistent with marketing applications; provide QA review of CMC sections of regulatory filings, post-approval supplements, and variations
* Establish and oversee commercial batch record review and lot disposition, ensuring final disposition complies with approved registrations and supporting QP certification for EU supply
* Build post-market quality processes, including product complaint handling, regulatory reporting (e.g., Field Alert Reports), recalls, and annual product quality reviews.
* Oversee quality requirements for commercial packaging, labeling, artwork control, and serialization (DSCSA and other market requirements)
* Ensure Good Distribution Practice (GDP) compliance for commercial distribution, including qualification of third-party logistics providers, temperature excursion management, and returns
* Where applicable, integrate combination product and device quality requirements (e.g., 21 CFR Part 4) for drug-device presentations
* Develop and lead risk-based quality oversight of CDMOs, contract testing laboratories, and other GMP suppliers, including qualification, audits, and performance management.
* Negotiate and maintain commercial Quality Agreements and ensure adherence by Kailera and its partners
* Use independent judgment to resolve highly complex or novel quality issues, such as major deviations, OOS investigations, and supply disruptions, balancing patient safety, compliance, and supply continuity
* Direct cross-functional, multidisciplinary teams across Technical Operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, and external partners to resolve quality events and implement improvements
* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing GMP Quality team as Kailera scales to commercial operations, including organizational design, hiring, and succession planning
* Drive followership by leading with trust, understanding, and adaptability; coach managers and team members, recognize contributions, and foster a culture of quality, accountability, and psychological safety
* Manage GMP Quality budget and resources, including the use of external consultants and auditors

 

**Required Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of GMP experience in the FDA-regulated pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry (or 10+ years with an advanced degree), including significant experience supporting commercial products
* Demonstrated success leading quality activities for product registration and commercial launch, including PPQ and PAI/PLI readiness
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including building and developing teams
* Expert knowledge of cGMP and GDP requirements, including 21 CFR Parts 210, 211, and 11, EudraLex Volume 4 (including Annex 16), and ICH Q7, Q9, and Q10; working knowledge of 21 CFR Part 4 and DSCSA preferred
* Track record of successfully hosting or supporting FDA, EMA, and/or other health authority inspections
* Extensive experience leading quality oversight of CDMOs and contract laboratories, including audits and Quality Agreements
* Proficient in Veeva QualityDocs and Veeva QMS or a comparable electronic quality system
* Recognized expertise in GMP quality, with the judgment to give clear, risk-based quality advice that balances compliance with business needs
* Exceptional communication skills; tailors messages to executives, cross-functional partners, contract manufacturers, and health authorities, and explains the rationale behind decisions to build buy-in
* Proven ability to guide teams through complex change and ambiguity, anticipate problems before they escalate, and keep work focused on defined outcomes in a fast-paced, growing company
* Builds trusting relationships internally and externally, and navigates conflict through open dialogue and collaboration
* Brings creative, practical solutions to complex problems and encourages others to take calculated risks that challenge the status quo while maintaining compliance

 

**Education:**

* BA or BS degree in a scientific discipline required; advanced degree preferred

**For Full Time Roles:** This range represents the company's good-faith estimate of the salary at the time of posting. Actual pay may vary based on experience, skills, qualifications, location, and internal equity. We also offer comprehensive health coverage, flexible time off, paid holidays, and a year-end shutdown. Enjoy a monthly wellness stipend, generous 401(k) match, tuition reimbursement, commuter benefits, disability and life insurance, plus annual bonus opportunities and equity grants—because your well-being and future matter to us.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY INFORMATION:**

Kailera Therapeutics, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, creed, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age (40 and over), sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, pregnancy-related conditions, and lactation), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, genetic information, reproductive health decisions, domestic victim status, political affiliation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances.

*E-Verify:*

Kailera Therapeutics, Inc. uses E-Verify to confirm the identity and employment eligibility of all new hires.

records.title: Director, Central Quality Audit, Pharmacovigilance
records.description:
**Job Description Summary**
===========================

Managing, ensuring and improving capabilities to comply with external standards and regulations. Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may influence work. 
 
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

**Job Description**
===================

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Own the Pharmacovigilance (PV) Audit Program: Develop, implement, and maintain the global PV audit strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations (e.g., EMA, FDA, MHRA, PMDA) and industry best practices.
* Manage Audit Operations: Oversee scheduling, planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up for PV audits, including internal audits and audits of service providers and affiliates. Fully participate in the audit program; actively owning and executing PV audits.
* Risk Identification and Communication: Identify high-risk compliance issues, escalate findings, and provide actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
* Regulatory Inspection Support: Prepare for and support PV-related health authority inspections, including back-room management and post-inspection follow-up.
* Metrics and Reporting: Define and track PV audit KPIs, ensuring visibility of compliance risks and trends to leadership.
* System Ownership: Manage audit-related modules within the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), including support of configuration, UAT, and documentation.
* Team Leadership: Lead and develop a team of 3–5 auditors, providing coaching, mentorship, and performance management.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with PV Operations, Quality, and Regulatory teams to ensure audit outcomes drive continuous improvement.
* Strategic Influence: Contribute to policy development and influence PV compliance strategy across the organization.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 5 years of people leadership experience, including team development and performance management.
* Qualified Lead Auditor with active certification.
* Master’s degree and 5+ years in pharmacovigilance or pharmaceutical industry; or Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years relevant experience.
* Minimum of 5 years’ experience driving Global programs to resolve quality compliance issues (directly).
* Experience with Pharmaceutical QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to cGMP, GDP, GPvP, GCP and GLP.

**Desired Characteristics**

* Experience with Medical Device QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to FDA CFR 21 820 and ISO 13485.
* Prior Veeva and TrackWise Digital experience a plus.
* Prior health authority experience a plus.
* IRCA, ASQ (CQE, CQA, etc.) and/or Lean Certification a plus (green belt, black belt).
* Extensive experience in the Medica Device and Pharmaceutical industry.
* Understanding of product quality improvement using tools such as Six Sigma, DFR.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems.
* Exceptional conflict-resolution skills.
* Ability to interface with top organizational leadership and internal and external customers, responding in a professional manner.
* Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects. Ability to prioritize and drive multiple programs.
* Ability to energize others by building a connection with the team through personal involvement and trust, providing feedback and coaching to develop others, and accountability of actions.
* Strong oral and written communication skills in English.
* Integrity: Accepting and adhering to high ethical, moral, and personal values in decisions, communications, actions, and when dealing with others.
* Ability to travel globally up to 15%.

We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership –always with unyielding integrity.

Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening. For U.S. based positions only, the pay range for this position is $142,400.00-$213,600.00 Annual. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the pay range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including skills, qualifications, experience and location. In addition, this position may also be eligible to earn performance based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonus(es) and/or long term incentives (LTI). GE HealthCare offers a competitive benefits package, including not but limited to medical, dental, vision, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employee and company contribution opportunities, life, disability, and accident insurance, and tuition reimbursement.

**Additional Information**
==========================

GE HealthCare offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE HealthCare will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable).

While GE HealthCare does not currently require U.S. employees to be vaccinated against COVID-19, some GE HealthCare customers have vaccination mandates that may apply to certain GE HealthCare employees.

**Relocation Assistance Provided:** No

Application Deadline: December 21, 2026

records.description:
Division Department: Therapeutics | Quality

Position Title: Director of Quality (Head of Quality)

Reports To: Corporate Head of Quality (proposed; final reporting structure to be confirmed)

Salary - $225-250,000 based on experience

**PharmaLogic is expanding our therapeutics business line. Our therapeutics business, Agilera, is the** **world’s only cGMP-compliant CDMO currently manufacturing and distributing commercial radiopharmaceutical therapeutics across more than 30 countries. In this role,** **you will have the opportunity to work as part of a unique environment that is involved in the entire value chain, from the preclinical phase to the commercial production and distribution of radiopharmaceuticals.**

**Role Summary:**

The Director of Quality serves as the Head of Quality for PharmaLogic’s newly acquired therapeutics business, leading the quality organization and establishing the systems, capabilities, and culture needed for reliable GMP manufacturing. This leader is accountable for the pharmaceutical quality system and Quality oversight of sterile therapeutic drug manufacturing, testing, and release under applicable 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 requirements. As a member of the site leadership team, the Director partners with Operations, Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, and corporate Quality to support clinical supply, technology transfer, commercialization, and growth. The role requires independent judgment, visible leadership on the manufacturing floor, and the ability to translate quality requirements into practical execution while protecting patient safety and product quality.

**Job Responsibilities and Duties:**

**Quality Leadership and Governance**

Lead the Quality function, including Quality Assurance and oversight of Quality Control and microbiology activities within the assigned organizational scope. Set strategy, staffing, budgets, objectives, and development plans; build a capable team with clear accountability.

Maintain the Quality unit’s independent authority to approve or reject materials and drug products, including outsourced products; approve quality-impacting procedures and specifications; and ensure documented responsibilities and appropriate escalation to corporate Quality and executive leadership.

Own batch disposition through authorized Quality personnel. Ensure production and laboratory records, deviations, and required test results receive appropriate review before release. Place materials or product on hold and stop affected operations when quality or compliance concerns warrant.

**Quality Systems and Sterile Manufacturing**

Establish and continuously improve systems for deviations, investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, document control, training, complaints, product quality reviews, and quality risk management. Require scientifically sound root-cause analysis and verification of CAPA effectiveness.

Provide Quality oversight of aseptic processing and contamination control, including cleanrooms, environmental and personnel monitoring, gowning qualification, aseptic process simulations, sterilization, disinfection, and container closure integrity, as applicable.

Oversee laboratory controls, specifications, analytical method validation and transfer, stability programs, and investigations of out-of-specification and out-of-trend results. Ensure complete, accurate, traceable data and effective controls for electronic records and computerized systems.

Approve qualification and validation strategies, protocols, and reports for facilities, utilities, equipment, manufacturing processes, cleaning, and computerized systems. Ensure a documented lifecycle approach and continued process verification.

**Manufacturing Readiness and External Partners**

Lead Quality readiness for new products, technology transfers, process scale-up, and commercial launches. Establish clear acceptance criteria and readiness decisions with Development, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.

Serve as the primary site Quality representative for FDA inspections and customer audits. Lead inspection preparation, responses, and commitments; maintain sustained readiness and timely, effective remediation.

Manage supplier qualification, contract laboratory and manufacturer oversight, audits, and quality agreements. Define responsibilities with CDMO customers and ensure outsourced activities meet agreed quality requirements.

**Acquisition Integration and Regulatory Partnership**

Lead the acquisition Quality integration plan: assess inherited systems and commitments, prioritize gaps by risk, align governance and procedures with corporate standards, and manage changes without disrupting compliant product supply.

Partner with Regulatory Affairs on manufacturing and quality content for filings, change assessments, and regulatory commitments. Lead quality defect assessments and support recalls, field actions, and required notifications with designated functions.

For radiopharmaceutical therapeutics, oversee appropriate controls for isotope and precursor quality, radiochemical testing, time-sensitive manufacturing and disposition, and stability. Partner with Radiation Safety and EHS on safe, compliant execution.

**Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement**

Present quality performance and material risks to site and corporate leadership. Use management reviews and meaningful metrics to improve investigation quality, CAPA effectiveness, release reliability, training, and inspection readiness.

**Job Requirements, Skills and Education:**

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, microbiology, pharmacy, engineering, or a related scientific discipline.

Typically, 10 or more years of progressive pharmaceutical Quality experience, including at least 5 years leading teams or major Quality programs in a GMP manufacturing environment.

Demonstrated Quality leadership in sterile injectable manufacturing, with substantial knowledge of aseptic processing, contamination control, laboratory controls, validation, and data integrity.

**Strong working knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, applicable electronic records requirements, and relevant FDA guidance and ICH quality principles.**

Experience leading regulatory inspections, complex investigations, remediation, and batch disposition, with sound scientific judgment and the ability to defend quality decisions.

Experience supporting technology transfer, clinical or commercial manufacturing, and cross-functional delivery of significant quality or operational improvements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Experience with therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals or radioligand therapies; CDMO operations and pharmaceutical customer partnerships; and commercial launch or preapproval inspection readiness.

Experience integrating an acquisition, building or transforming a quality organization, and implementing electronic quality management systems. Advanced scientific degree or relevant professional certification.

**Leadership and Working Expectations**

A visible, hands-on leader who develops people, communicates clearly, and holds teams accountable. Able to challenge decisions constructively, escalate risks promptly, and make timely decisions under pressure. Regular onsite presence in manufacturing and laboratory areas, compliance with required gowning and safety practices, and availability for critical quality events are expected. Travel requirements will be defined for the role. Essential functions may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

Come join our winning team and begin a fulfilling career with us by applying today. 
 
PharmaLogic is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other protected class.

**Benefits Include:**

401(k) retirement benefit program

Medical

Dental care

Disability insurance

Employee assistance program

Life insurance

On-site parking

Paid time off

Vision care
