records.title: Plant Manager (Yokosuka, Japan)
records.description:
**NORESCO, an OPTERRA Company**, helps customers modernize aging building systems and upgrade energy and water infrastructure to meet evolving demands. We implement innovative energy efficiency, distributed generation, energy storage, and renewable energy solutions that optimize the operational efficiency and improve resilience of buildings, campuses, military installations, and communities.

We are seeking an on-site Project Manager to oversee all preventive, corrective, and major maintenance activities (including repair and replacement work) at NORESCO’s 40 MW electric and thermal production facility at Yokosuka Naval Base, Japan. The cogeneration plant (CGS) is a critical asset for the base and daily operations are conducted by Navy personnel in partnership with NORESCO and our subcontractors.

NORESCO constructed the plant, which generates 50Hz and 60Hz power as well as a combination of Soft and Pure Steam, in 2008 under a Federal Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC). The plant pays for itself out of energy savings which NORESCO has guaranteed for the past 18 years. In order to meet our savings and availability guarantees, we employ a robust preventive maintenance program which relies heavily on Long Term Service Agreements (LTSAs) for all major pieces of equipment.

This is a Senior level position reporting to NORESCO’s Operations Manager and is administered through a 3 to 5 year International Assignment Agreement (IAA). This agreement is negotiated with each of our employees working Outside of the Continental Unites States (OCONUS). The agreement includes consideration for overseas pay, benefits, healthcare, housing, food, travel, vacation, stateside visits, relocation, etc., and is customized to the unique requirements of each new hire.

You will be the primary liaison between our NAVY customers, Japanese operators and subcontractors, as well as NORESCO team to ensure contractual obligations are met. While many of the team members in Japan speak English or are Bi-Lingual, some are not. Translators are available to facilitate conversations or process written correspondence as necessary. Japan is an amazing culture with many unique customs and protocols, a willingness to learn and adapt to their approach is an important part of your success.

It is of utmost importance for you to possess good listening, communication, and computer skills in addition to being proactive, organized, and having a bias for action. The Yokosuka Project Manager is supported by (and in-turn supports) many other NORESCO departments; Development, Engineering, Commissioning, O&M, M&V, Accounting, Legal, etc. Cross-functional technical skills, adaptability, versatility, and a quest for continuous learning and integration of advances are key in this position.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Overall contractual responsibility for plant maintenance and repair activities through careful management of Long-Term Service Agreements (LTSAs) and work orders.
* Ensuring subcontractor work is performed in a safe and professional manner with materials that meet or exceed applicable Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Regulatory standards.
* Participate in scheduled operations meetings and coordinate upcoming maintenance activities within the defined expectations and constraints of the customer and subcontractor availability.
* Prepare and distribute standard monthly reports (that summarize operations, maintenance, and repair activities) to NORESCO management, key customer contacts, and other stakeholders.
* Review plant operations logs, alarms, and performance data on a regular basis to evaluate equipment condition, collaborate with NORESCO team to identify potential issues.
* Perform plant inspections and safety walkthroughs during regular operations, confirm changes in equipment line-up, and subcontractor compliance with typical maintenance activities.
* Support Profit and Loss (P&L) management; assist with generating and maintaining the annual budget; capital expenditure planning; monthly forecasts, accruals, and variance analysis with development of recovery plans as needed to deliver the target revenue and profit.
* Review service agreements/proposals with manager; generate purchase orders as required; provide initial review and approval of invoices for materials and services.
* Collaborate with LTSA contractors to plan work and identify resources required for shutdown tasks such as parts, tooling, equipment, materials, and work procedures. Review and confirm subcontractors’ detailed work plans meet the customer and project needs.
* Maintain NORESCO’s Computer Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to generate reports for maintenance schedules, completion status reports, equipment histories, and forecasts.
* Coordinate with subcontractors, visitors and customers to ensure protocols are followed on matters related to site access, security clearance, safety measures, and work permits.
* Monitor warranty programs to ensure the planned and required coverage is maintained by complying with all warranty requirements. Ensure warranty work is claimed in a timely manner, and all warranty issues are resolved to minimize out of pocket expenses.
* Monitor and analyze facility performance and host data for equipment and systems condition assessments. Review finings with Operations Manger and adjust maintenance plans accordingly.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelors degree, Associates degree, or equivalent Technical Training (ex; Navy Nuclear)
* 5+ years of experience in one of the following fields; electric power generation, cogeneration, industrial utility, or district energy industry with strong working knowledge of equipment
* Ability to obtain a Federal Security Clearance for work at Government facilities.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**:

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, project management discipline or equivalent experience
* High level communication, leadership, technical, and project management skills.
* Strong sense of ownership and focus on maintaining; a Safe work environment, Uninterrupted Plant operations, Quality control, Project schedule, Resolving issues in a timely manner, and consistently meeting deadlines and commitments.
* Graduate degree in engineering or business administration
* Strong interest in engaging operators, customers, and partners to grow relationships.
* Advanced knowledge of one or more facets of Engineering or Central Plants operations; design principles, technologies, equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.
* Energy optimization, utility rates, energy costs, applicable codes, design guides, and standards.
* Robust combination of business acumen, risk management, and strategic thinking skills.
* US military or DOD project management experience, Japanese language skills, and international work experience are a plus.

**Physical requirements include:**

* Ability to climb stairs and fixed ladders.
* Ability to access rooftops and elevated work areas while following safety protocols.
* Ability to work at heights and in confined or industrial environments as required.
* Ability to maintain balance and mobility while navigating mechanical, utility, and production areas.

**Compensation:**

* $130,000 – $150,000 per year, depending on experience + bonuses

**Benefits:**

* HSA Medical insurance, with a choice of 2 buy-up options
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* 100% Safe Harbor 401(k) match
* 100% company paid Life insurance
* 100% company paid Long-term Disability insurance
* Short-term Disability insurance
* Flexible Spending Account
* Commuter Benefits
* Legal and Identity Protection
* Pet Insurance Coverage
* Fertility and Reproductive Health
* Generous Paid Time Off, including Holiday, Vacation, and Sick Pay

records.description:
**About the role:**
-------------------

As Plant Manager for Eaton’s Critical Power Solutions operations in Santa Ana, California, you’ll lead two facilities, 500+ employees, and approximately $280M in annual sales, delivering engineered-to-order critical power solutions for some of the world’s fastest-growing customers.

This is a **high-visibility business and operations leadership role** with the opportunity to make a significant impact. You’ll co-own the P&L, lead the full plant organization, and help scale the operation as demand continues to grow.

**We’re looking for a leader who can:**

* Build and develop high-performing, cross-functional teams.
* Deliver consistently against safety, quality, delivery, inventory, cost, and financial commitments.
* Create a culture of structured problem solving using A3, 8D, PDCA, and root cause analysis.
* Lead through growth, complexity, and change while maintaining strong operational discipline.
* Make sound financial decisions around cost, budgets, capital, capacity, and profitability.
* Move comfortably between the manufacturing floor, customer conversations, and senior leadership discussions.

**What you will do:**
---------------------

**Lead people and culture** 

* Build a safety-first culture where every employee owns EHS, and keep our safety management systems strong through active, visible leadership.
* Be a visible leader on every shift: communicate openly, spend real time on the floor, and build an inclusive team where people want to stay and grow.
* Model Eaton's values and Code of Ethics in how results get delivered, every day.

**Run a high-performing operation** 

* Co-own the site P&L and scorecard (safety, quality, delivery, inventory, cost, productivity and engagement), set stretch goals and close gaps quickly.
* Turn the division strategy and annual profit plan into clear short- and long-term site plans and run a disciplined daily management rhythm to deliver them.
* Lead demand, capacity and inventory planning (our Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning process) so we keep our commitments to customers and to the business.

**Put customers first** 

* Protect on-time delivery and shorten engineered-to-order and configure-to-order lead times so we win new business and grow with our customers.
* Partner with Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Project Management and Supply Chain to deliver end-to-end quality and customer satisfaction.

**Improve continuously** 

* Use the Eaton Business System and our continuous improvement tools to make lasting gains in safety, quality and productivity.
* Develop lean experts and problem-solvers on every shift, coach leaders to teach problem solving, and recognize teams that improve their own work.

**Grow the site** 

* Lead capacity expansion and footprint plans, including capital projects, new lines and cell layouts, automation and new product launches with Engineering.
* Represent Eaton in the Santa Ana community and build strong relationships with local stakeholders.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

**Basic qualifications** 

* Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, industrial operations, or similar fields.
* Minimum 7 years of experience with progressive levels of accountability and responsibility in Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, operational excellence (OPEX) and/or related support functions in a manufacturing environment.

 
**Preferred qualifications** 

* Master's in business administration (MBA) or other master's degree from an accredited institution.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma certification (Green Belt, Black Belt or Lean Tool Expert), with a track record of deploying a continuous improvement system.

• Strong understanding of Engineered to Order (ETO) and Configure to Order (CTO) business • Strong MRP / ERP platform knowledge, such as SAP or Oracle. 

* Bilingual (English and Spanish).

**Additional Information:**
---------------------------

* This role will be based at our manufacturing plant in Santa Ana, California.
* Relocation will be offered for this position.
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment, immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.
* Travel required up to 25% (domestic).

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

At Eaton, we strive to provide compensation and benefits that attract, engage, and retain the best talent. This includes competitive pay and a variety of benefit programs for eligible employees. The expected annual salary range for this role is $190000 - $278000 a year. This role is also eligible for a variable incentive program. *Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click here for more detail: Eaton Benefits Overview. Please note that specific programs and options available to an employee may depend on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

records.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.

**LOCATION:** Remote with Travel

US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.

This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.

The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**KEY PERFORMANCE METRICS:**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the essential duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job. Incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented.

records.title: Head of Operations / COO
records.description:
### **About the Role**

A seed-stage AI company serving manufacturers is hiring a Head of Operations / COO to own day-to-day business operations. Working closely with the founders, you will connect customer delivery, supplier and freight operations, and product priorities as the business grows.

### **What You'll Do**

* Own customer onboarding, order execution, supplier and carrier coordination, and issue resolution.
* Build the processes, metrics, and playbooks needed to serve more manufacturers with a lean team.
* Work with engineering to identify which operational workflows AI agents should automate next.
* Manage supplier and freight operations, vendor relationships, and service quality.
* Hire and lead the operations team as the company grows.
* Partner with the founders on planning, finance, and company priorities.

### **What We're Looking For**

* Six to ten years of professional experience, including senior operations leadership as a Head of Operations, COO, VP or Director of Operations, or in a similar role.
* Hands-on experience in supply chain, procurement, logistics, or manufacturing operations.
* Experience at an early-stage startup or on a small team, with the ability to build processes from the ground up and stay hands-on.
* Strong numerical, systems, and process-design skills.
* Experience in CPG, food, supplements, cosmetics, chemicals, or related manufacturing, or at a company serving those industries, is useful.
* Freight brokerage or 3PL experience, or experience as a founder or early startup employee, is a plus.

### **Location**

On-site in San Francisco, five days a week. Relocation within the United States is possible.

records.title: Director of Offshore Operations
records.description:
**About Endurance**
===================

Endurance is building the world's first modular subsea geothermal power plants, converting vast thermal resources under the ocean into gigawatts of baseload power. Backed by Founders Fund, Felicis, First Round Capital, and Point72 Ventures, our founding team includes veterans from SpaceX, Helion, Blue Origin, and Apple. We have completed multiple deep-ocean deployments to subsea volcanoes and are launching a long-term demonstration project this fall. By leveraging modular design, manufacturing scale, efficient drilling, and latent cooling on the seafloor, we are pioneering a new category of energy that outperforms traditional sources on environmental impact, deployment speed, and cost.

**Responsibilities**

* Own offshore readiness and execution end to end: plan each campaign from mission objectives through vessel, equipment, crew, schedule, and budget, and deliver it safely, on time, and at cost
* Select vessels for each mission: translate mission requirements into vessel requirements for deck space and strength, lifting capacity, station keeping, accommodation, and endurance; evaluate and inspect candidates; make the trade between capability, availability, and cost
* Negotiate and manage charter agreements and offshore service contracts; understand the day rates, liabilities, and terms that drive total campaign cost, and hold vessel owners and contractors to them
* Own marine insurance for our vessels, equipment, and operations; work directly with brokers, underwriters, and marine warranty surveyors, and make sure our engineering and procedures meet their requirements
* Personally perform the design and analysis for equipment mobilizations: deck layouts, seafastening and grillage design, lift plans, vessel stability and motions, and launch and recovery loads; know when independent review or class approval is required and obtain it without losing schedule
* Plan and lead mobilizations and demobilizations: port selection, shipping and customs, installation on deck, function testing, and readiness reviews before the vessel leaves the dock
* Own maintenance and readiness of all offshore assets, including ROVs, drilling systems, launch and recovery equipment, and rigging; establish maintenance programs, spares, and certifications so equipment works when it reaches site
* Define staffing for offshore campaigns and asset maintenance: decide what we hire, contract, and train; establish crew plans, rotations, and competency requirements; recruit and lead the team as it grows
* Lead campaigns offshore as the senior Endurance representative: direct operations with the vessel master and crew, make weather and operability decisions, resolve problems as they occur, and turn each campaign's lessons into better equipment and procedures
* Move aggressively while maintaining exceptional technical rigor and safe operations: set the standard for risk assessments and offshore procedures, surface risks immediately, and drive recovery rather than wait for clean requirements or instructions

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in naval architecture, ocean, mechanical, or structural engineering, or a related engineering discipline
* 10+ years of experience in offshore operations, subsea construction, marine installation, or a comparably demanding offshore environment
* A record of leading offshore campaigns as the person accountable for the outcome, including time at sea directing operations
* Experience personally performing mobilization engineering, such as deck layouts, seafastening design, and lift planning, not only reviewing the work of others
* Direct experience selecting and chartering vessels, including negotiating charter terms with vessel owners and brokers
* Experience owning the maintenance and operational readiness of offshore equipment, with independent responsibility for technical and commercial decisions under uncertainty
* Willingness and ability to spend around two months per year offshore, to travel regularly beyond that to vessels, ports, and suppliers, and to obtain the required offshore medical and safety certifications

**Preferred Skills and Experience**

* Degree or professional background in naval architecture, with hands-on experience in vessel stability, motions analysis, and structural analysis of deck equipment and foundations
* Experience operating and maintaining work-class ROVs, subsea or seabed drilling systems, and launch and recovery systems
* Experience working with marine warranty surveyors, classification societies, and marine insurers to gain approval for offshore operations
* Experience executing campaigns from remote ports, including international shipping, customs, and local port and agent logistics
* Experience with deepwater operations, heavy subsea lifts, or installation of large equipment on the seafloor

• • A record of building an offshore operations function or team at a small or fast-growing company, including hiring, contracting, and crewing

**Compensation, Benefits, & Perks**
===================================

As a pre-revenue startup, Endurance Energy offers competitive base salaries and generous equity packages for full-time employees. Final base salary will be determined by an array of factors including internal equity, job-related knowledge, skills, and work experience.

A key aspect of our compensation philosophy is that value creation should be aligned with rewards. Right now this means equity is a significant portion of every full-time employee's compensation. As the company matures, there will be continued evolution and changes to the total rewards and total compensation package. What will always be true is that if we win, we win together. Equity is granted to every full-time employee as a meaningful piece of ownership. We believe the people building the company should share directly in the value they create.

In addition to a competitive base salary and equity, employees will receive all of our other great benefits and perks, including:

* **Benefits**: Health, Dental, and Vision insurance coverage
* **Time Away:** Flexible PTO including 12 paid company holidays
* **Global Fieldwork**: Travel to fascinating deployment sites along oceanic ridges in locations like the Pacific Northwest, Hawaii, Iceland, Japan, New Zealand, and the Azores
* **Hands-on Experience**: Participate in sea trials and deployment operations in partnership with leading oceanographic institutions
* **Cutting-edge Development**: Work with technology that spans high-power electronics, marine systems, and clean energy
* **Impactful Work**: Help solve one of the world's most pressing challenges
* **Dive Certification**: Company-sponsored recreational dive certification
* **Other Perks:** Access to the company boat, free meals and snacks, and the list goes on!

If you’re selected for consideration, a recruiter will be able to discuss in greater detail.

Compensation Range: $225K - $275K

records.title: Senior Manager, Weatherization Quality & Technical Services

postedPay.title: Senior Manager, Weatherization Quality & Technical Services

records.description:
**Department Information**
--------------------------

The mission of the Colorado Energy Office (CEO) is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and consumer energy costs by advancing clean energy, energy efficiency, and zero emission vehicles to benefit all Coloradans. We do this by developing and implementing highly impactful policies and programs, establishing Colorado as a leading state for climate action. The Colorado Energy Office is a great place to work, with collaborative and talented employees who are passionate about our mission and a hybrid atmosphere. Employees report high satisfaction with their work, their colleagues and manager, and CEO leadership. Join us!

 
 

Reducing greenhouse gas pollution and advancing zero emission vehicles, energy efficiency and clean energy are essential to preserving and protecting Colorado’s way of life. These actions defend the health of our communities and natural environment, provide access to lower cost clean energy resources for rural and urban areas, increase investment and economic growth opportunities, and expand clean energy jobs. As part of our mission we serve the people of Colorado with programs focusing on weatherization, energy efficiency, and electric vehicles and a regulatory and legislative agenda to promote the interests of all Coloradans.

 
 

***We are committed to increasing the diversity of our staff and providing culturally responsive programs and services. Therefore, we encourage responses from people of all backgrounds and abilities.***

**Description of Job**
----------------------

* **This is a hybrid position. Hybrid positions are required to be present at the office location for a minimum of two days per work week during the first 90 days, and minimum one to two days a week after that, or as directed by office leadership.**

CEO’s Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), helps qualified Coloradans save money, increase comfort, and better their homes and environment through proven energy conservation solutions.These solutions include LED light bulbs, high efficiency furnaces and refrigerators, building shell insulation, and rooftop solar arrays, among others.

 
 

CEO is hiring for a visionary Senior Manager, Weatherization Quality & Technical Services to join the WAP team. You will serve as a strategic leader, bridging advanced building science with organizational excellence. This role is pivotal in shaping how we deliver sustainable energy solutions to diverse communities across Colorado, turning technical compliance into a platform for continuous improvement and innovation.

The WAP network spans all 64 Colorado counties, delivering critical energy efficiency and clean energy solutions to diverse populations through a network of six subgrantee agencies. As the Senior Manager, you will step into a high-impact, supervisory role overseeing a team of technical experts located around the state who serve as the definitive authority on residential building science, ensuring weatherization work meets performance standards through on-site inspections, detailed reporting, and training, while also acting as an internal and network consultant to streamline operations, drive process improvement, and ensure program delivery is transparent and visible.

 
 

In this senior-level manager capacity, you will blend advanced building science knowledge with administrative leadership and process optimization.

WAP Specific Duties and Responsibilities

* Lead the Quality Management team, which includes Technical & QCI Quality Management staff in completing all necessary BPI certified Quality Assurance Inspections (typically 50-75/yr) and Quality Control visits (typically 20-30/yr) across Colorado to meet all federal and state statutory and programmatic requirements
* Balance the team’s core focus (QA, QC, & training) with opportunities for ongoing innovation.
* Drive strategic quality management through Quality Control and Assurance (QC & QA), transforming federal guidelines into accessible, actionable insights that empower our subgrantee network
* Cultivate a high-performing team by providing mentorship and leadership that fosters a collaborative, inclusive environment where technical experts can thrive and innovate
* Partner with other CEO WAP teams to integrate quality management operational outcomes with targeted training to drive continuous, lasting enhancements across the program
* Lead the QM team in partnering with other CEO WAP teams to develop and deliver targeted, hands-on guidance to local subgrantee organizations undergoing leadership shifts or performance remediation, ensuring full alignment with state and federal guidelines, state program implementation strategies, and complementary clean energy initiatives
* Champion Operational Excellence by collaborating cross-functionally with other CEO WAP teams to identify bottlenecks, modernize our workflows, and scale our program’s reach
* Provide immediate support to subgrantees to address critical safety hazards detected during site evaluations or staff reviews, escalating severe concerns to WAP Director when subgrantee remediation or corrective action is warranted
* Work with the rest of the WAP team on QM production metrics from subgrantee agencies, auditing subgrantee performance for integrity and collaborating cross-functionally to report key outcomes to program leadership, federal partners, state administrators, and legislative bodies
* Influence Program Strategy by serving as a key advisor in creating WAP policy, translating real-world QM data into meaningful policy updates that increase program equity and effectiveness
* Modernize Tooling by leading the integration and management of platforms like monday.com to create transparent, streamlined project tracking systems and program delivery improvements.
* Participate in national and regional WAP events hosted by national associations to learn from and elevate the work of Colorado WAP

General Duties and Responsibilities

* Adhere to all technical and health and safety policies and procedures in the planning and execution of activities
* Maintain positive working relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders including WAP subgrantee agency staff, CEO Ops and Finance team, Federal Department of Energy partners, among others
* Abide by office policies and procedures in a manner that ensures fiscal responsibility and promotes efficient, effective, and elegant government.
* Use application software (i.e. word processing, spreadsheet, database, project management software, etc.) to prepare correspondence, plans, reports, schedules, and other documents
* Assist other CEO departments in carrying out unit and office wide priorities.
* Perform other duties as requested and required

**Supplemental Information**
----------------------------

We are looking for an experienced manager who pairs technical building science awareness with sophisticated team leadership expertise and continuous improvement approach.

Minimum Qualifications

* Minimum 2 years of direct supervisory experience OR similar translatable experience (indirect supervision like volunteer management, mentorship, vendor or contractor management)
* Minimum three years of working, inspection, and/or training experience in weatherization, residential energy efficiency services, or closely related field

Skills and Knowledge 
 

* Demonstrated ability to use the virtual collaboration strategies and tools necessary to lead a distributed team
* Demonstrated experience tracking compliance, reviewing staff reporting, and processing/approving invoices
* Dedicated to continuous improvement, desire to learn new skills
* Demonstrated leadership and facilitation capabilities
* Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
* Strong interpersonal skills with a focus on developing strong relationships
* Ability to independently start and finish tasks
* Ability to work independently and as part of a team
* Strong written, oral, and presentation communication skills
* Willingness to adapt to and enhance current team culture
* Proficient in the following:

 + Google Suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Gmail, Calendar, etc.) or Microsoft equivalent
 + Video conferencing software (Zoom, Google Meet, MS Teams, etc.)
* Experience and/or a willingness to use AI tools and best practices to inform programs and program management.

Preferred Qualifications

* Direct supervisory experience in the last five years
* Possession of or ability to obtain the Quality Control Inspector (QCI) certification within twelve months of hire date, see this PDF download for more information
* Experience using Salesforce
* Project Management software experience (i.e. Monday.com, Asana, etc.)
* Professional experience in sustainability, climate policy, or clean energy

 
Interested in learning more about:

* Process Improvement Methodologies (i.e Lean/Six Sigma)
* Total Quality Management (TQM)
* Colorado Energy Industry

records.title: Senior Manager Operational Excellence Initiatives
records.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

**Position Summary**

CVS is seeking a Senior Manager to own the end-to-end process and technology strategy for stocking and picking across CVS Distribution. This role sits within the Operational Excellence (OpEx) Initiatives team, reporting to the Executive Director of Operational Excellence Initiatives (whose peers lead the OpEx Regional and OpEx Analytics organizations), alongside three other Senior Managers and a team of Managers/Senior Analysts. This role has two direct reports. Where peer Senior Managers on the team own the inbound-through-machine-replenishment and inbound/outbound value streams, this role owns the network's stocking and picking processes – the highest-volume and most labor-intensive processes in our network. This individual will also serve as the process-side subject matter expert on Warehouse Management System (WMS) configuration within owned value streams, to ensure system and process are in alignment. The role requires approximately 30–50% travel, often in stretches on an every-other-week cadence.

Responsibilities:

* **Technology Deployment (50%) —** Own the 3-year technology roadmap for stocking, picking, and module support, including code updates to existing processes, new process rollouts, and major enhancements, to improve colleague experience, quality, and productivity.
* + **Success Measures** — Deliver measurable improvements in inventory accuracy, stocking and picking quality defects, and throughput, specific to each enhancement or process change.
* **Process Optimization (15%) —** Own the process and technology, and advise on WMS configuration needs within your value streams, working with the other subject matter experts on the team who consult on and implement WMS changes, to tune system settings, improve operations, and keep WMS, technology, and process aligned across stocking and picking:
* + **Stocking —** Own the process and core technology for replenishing split-case picking modules
* + **Picking —** Own the process and core technology for picking across multiple picking methods, including split case and full case, in both active pick slots and reserve storage locations
* **Project & Change Management (25%) —** Plan and execute multiple concurrent projects (typically 4–5 programs in parallel, with a rollout roughly every other week across approximately 2,000 associates), applying strong project management skills — managing risk, critical path, dependencies, and budget — to meet project goals on time. Larger programs are led by the network Center of Excellence (COE); on others, this role provides oversight while the site leads. Build the financial business case and project plan for new opportunities, and ensure robust follow-through on changes to sustain results.
* **Mentorship/Training (10%)—** Grow and shape the organization's lean capability, developing training content and standard work that enhances the continuous improvement culture across the network. Lead, coach, and develop direct reports.

This is a work-from-home role with travel; relocation is not offered. The ideal candidate is located near one of the following distribution centers: La Habra (CA), Patterson (CA), Conroe (TX), Lumberton (NJ), Woonsocket (RI), Chemung (NY), Novi (DT), Kansas City (MO), Indianapolis (IN), Orlando (FL), North Augusta (SC), Fredericksburg (VA), or Knoxville (TN).

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related engineering/science field or additional 4 years of experience in the requirements below
* 6+ years' experience in a manufacturing or distribution center environment
* 4+ years of demonstrated success and experience in Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, or Operational Excellence in a manufacturing or warehouse operation
* 4+ years of demonstrated success in managing projects
* 4+ years of experience with WMS, ERP, MES, or LMS systems and database structure

* 2+ years of experience with SQL
* Proven ability to influence and partner with operations, IT, and finance leaders; strong written and verbal communication; self-motivated and effective at managing multiple priorities 
 
 **Preferred Qualifications**
* 9+ years' experience in a manufacturing or distribution center environment
* 6+ years as continuous improvement, industrial engineering, or process engineering
* 2+ years of experience with Microsoft Azure Snowflake semantic modeling and Power BI
* 2+ years running operations (plant manager, senior operations manager, etc.)
* Certified in standards-based time and motion study systems such as MOST and MTM
* APICS CPIM, CSCP, or CLTD Certified
* PMP Certified
* Six Sigma Black Belt Certified

**Pay Range**

The typical pay range for this role is:

$82,940.00 - $182,549.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

**Great benefits for great people**

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

 
This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.

Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.

 
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 12/14/2026

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

records.title: Senior Manager - Biomanufacturing, Manufacturing Technical Operations
records.description:
**About Site**
--------------

Catalent’s Madison, Wisconsin site is a state‑of‑the‑art biologics development and manufacturing facility supporting customers from research through early‑ and mid‑stage clinical production. Located at 726 Heartland Trail in Madison, the approximately 102,700‑square‑foot GMP facility specializes in mammalian cell line engineering, drug substance biomanufacturing, and biopharmaceutical development, utilizing flexible single‑use systems to enable rapid scale‑up and customization. The site is home to Catalent’s proprietary GPEx® and GPEx® Lightning technologies, which are used to generate high‑yielding mammalian cell lines for biologic therapies, and supports production scales ranging from 50 to 4,000 liters for clinical manufacturing. Following a $45 million expansion announced in 2025, the Madison site has significantly increased capacity, added new equipment, and created approximately 200 highly skilled biohealth jobs, further strengthening its role within Catalent’s global biologics network and Wisconsin’s growing life sciences ecosystem.

**Position Summary**
--------------------

We have an opportunity for a Senior Manager - Biomanufacturing, Manufacturing Technical Operations to join our team. This role leads the Manufacturing Technical Operations organization, including Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Manufacturing Training. The position ensures safe, compliant, and reliable biomanufacturing operations while driving continuous improvement and technical excellence. The successful candidate will help strengthen workforce capability, reduce operational risk, and ensure sustainable preventive solutions across manufacturing operations.

Shift: Monday - Friday 8:00AM - 5:00PM 
Location: Madison, WI 
100% Onsite

**The Role**
------------

* Lead, coach, develop, and evaluate leaders and technical professionals supporting Manufacturing Engineering, Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Training.
* Establish clear goals, role accountabilities, performance expectations, succession plans, and development strategies for the organization.
* Provide organizational ownership for Manufacturing-based engineering support and technical response to process, equipment, materials, automation, documentation, and execution issues.
* Establish and govern a structured Rapid Response Team process that defines the problem, operational impact, containment, technical resources, decision ownership, recovery plan, communications, and escalation pathway.
* Provide leadership and oversight for Manufacturing deviation investigations, including investigation quality, aging, cycle time, right-first-time approval, and recurring-event reduction.
* Ensure investigations are fact-based and clearly distinguish event description, product and process impact, root cause, contributing factors, correction, corrective action, and preventive action.
* Establish Manufacturing Technical Operations as a key owner and contributor to process readiness, including batch production record review, dry runs, equipment readiness, material availability, qualification status, and execution-risk review.
* Ensure new equipment is transitioned into routine use with defined operational ownership, procedures, training, spare parts, maintenance, and troubleshooting strategies.
* Establish an integrated performance-management system using measures such as recurrence, recovery time, repeat failures, downtime, deviation aging, investigation right-first-time performance, corrective and preventive action aging and effectiveness, qualification progress, equipment reliability, open risks, and project delivery.
* Use performance data to establish priorities, allocate resources, escalate risk, and hold leaders accountable for outcomes.

**The Candidate**
-----------------

### **Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Biotechnology, Biological Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required.
* Ten (10) or more years of relevant manufacturing, engineering, technical operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology, Quality, or related experience.
* Five (5) or more years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for technical professionals, people leaders, or manufacturing-support organizations.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex technical problem solving and operational recovery in a Good Manufacturing Practice manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience with deviation investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, root-cause analysis, inspection readiness, and quality risk management.
* Advanced understanding of current Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including upstream, downstream, solution-preparation, equipment, and support systems.
* Demonstrable leadership experience at Catalent (including but not limited to participation in Catalent‑sponsored leadership programs such as Next Generation Global Leaders, GOLD, LEAD Now, General Manager Excellence, and GROW) may be considered in place of external experience.

### **Preferred Skills & Background**

* Advanced degree preferred.
* Experience in Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

**Why You Should Join Catalent**
--------------------------------

* Defined career path and annual performance review and feedback process.
* Diverse, inclusive culture.
* Potential for career growth on an expanding team within an organization dedicated to preserving and bettering lives.
* Competitive paid time off plus 8 paid holidays.
* Community engagement and green initiatives.
* Medical, dental, and vision benefits effective day one of employment.
* Tuition reimbursement.

**Catalent offers rewarding opportunities to further your career!** Join the global drug development and delivery leader and help us bring over 7,000 life-saving and life-enhancing products to patients around the world. Catalent is an exciting and growing international company where employees work directly with pharma, biopharma and consumer health companies of all sizes to advance new medicines from early development to clinical trials and to the market. Catalent produces more than 70 billion doses per year, and each one will be used by someone who is counting on us. Join us in making a difference.

personal initiative. dynamic pace. meaningful work.

Visit Catalent Careers to explore career opportunities.

Catalent is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and veterans.

If you require reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process due to a disability, you may submit your request by sending an email, and confirming your request for an accommodation and include the job number, title and location to DisabilityAccommodations@catalent.com. This option is reserved for individuals who require accommodation due to a disability. Information received will be processed by a U.S. Catalent employee and then routed to a local recruiter who will provide assistance to ensure appropriate consideration in the application or hiring process.

Notice to Agency and Search Firm Representatives: Catalent Pharma Solutions (Catalent) is not accepting unsolicited resumes from agencies and/or search firms for this job posting. Resumes submitted to any Catalent employee by a third party agency and/or search firm without a valid written & signed search agreement, will become the sole property of Catalent. No fee will be paid if a candidate is hired for this position as a result of an unsolicited agency or search firm referral. Thank you.

Important Security Notice to U.S. Job Seekers:

Catalent NEVER asks candidates to provide any type of payment, bank details, photocopies of identification, social security number or other highly sensitive personal information during the offer process, and we NEVER do so via email or social media. If you receive any such request, DO NOT respond— it is a fraudulent request. Please forward such requests to spam@catalent.com for us to investigate with local authorities.

California Job Seekers can find our California Job Applicant Notice HERE.

**Volunteer Work Disclosure:** Applicants for employment in Massachusetts may include in their employment history any verified work performed on a volunteer basis.

**Massachusetts Lie Detector Test Notice:** It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law may be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. Consistent with Massachusetts law, Catalent does not require or administer lie detector tests as a condition of employment or continued employment.

records.title: Quality Engineering Sr Manager - L6
records.description:
**Standard Job Description**
----------------------------

Manages those who apply quality principles in the areas of: design, incoming material, production control, product evaluation, program performance, reliability, inventory control, and/or research and development as they apply to product or process quality for make and/or buy products. Performs technical evaluations including product requirements, specifications, models/designs, drawings and procedures. Collaborates with program management, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain and customers on quality related issues to ensure quality standards are in place. Engages in product failure investigations, material review board decisions and corrective/preventive action. Ensures corrective measures meet acceptable reliability standards and/or are compliant with requirements. Develops strategies and systems designed to improve internal and/or supplier performance and productivity. Evaluates quality systems for deficiency identification and correction. Designs and analyzes inspection and testing processes, mechanisms and equipment; conducts product quality tests, performs statistical analysis to assess products or materials that do not meet required standards and specifications. Engages in supplier selection process and maintain certification programs.

**Basic Qualifications**
------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college
* 10 years of leadership experience
* 8 years flightline/flight test operations experience
* Quality experience - either in a quality organization or with significant exposure to quality processes
* Ability to travel

**Desired Skills**
------------------

* Prior leadership experience in a unionized workforce environment
* AS9100/9110 experience
* Ability to interpret military service guidance
* Understanding of DCMAI 8210.1 (all revisions)
* Demonstrated ability to work in a blended environment with contractor & gov’t personnel - both military and civilian
* Experience developing BOE through negotiation and contract award
* Interpersonal skills required to develop effective working relationships
* Excellent presentation skills/ability to effectively communicate at all levels of the organization

**Pay Information**

Full-Time Salary Range: $178500.00 - $331500.00

At Lockheed Martin, we know mission success starts with taking care of our people. Our Total Rewards program is designed to attract top talent, support your well-being, and help you grow—both professionally and personally.

records.title: Senior Manager, US Quality Operations
records.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.

With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.

As production grows, we need clear evidence that each spacecraft meets its requirements and a quality system that helps teams find and resolve risks early.

We are looking for a **Senior Manager, Quality Operations** to lead US quality for satellite buses and payloads from incoming material through building, test and acceptance. You will build a pragmatic system and lead engineers and inspectors close to the floor. You have independent authority to hold work or withhold readiness concurrence and to escalate unresolved mission risk. This is a hands-on leadership role in a fast-moving, dynamic environment.

**What you will do:**
=====================

* Lead US quality engineers and inspectors across supplier, receiving, production and test coverage. Set training, inspection points and delegated authority.
* Own fit-for-stage quality controls for document and configuration records, serial and lot traceability, calibration, nonconformances, corrective action and acceptance packages.
* Define risk-based controls for critical characteristics and supplier parts. Work with Supply Chain on qualifications, escapes, containment and verified corrective action.
* Make quality status visible through yield, repeat defects, escapes, NCR aging and acceptance-record completeness. Use trends to improve controls with Manufacturing and Engineering.
* Own the quality hold and escalation process. Engineering owns technical disposition; Quality evaluates controls and evidence and concurs on release.
* Concur independently on quality evidence at acceptance and flight readiness reviews. Escalate residual risk despite schedule pressure; partner with Engineering on reliability and mission risk.
* Align common requirements with the Canada Quality Lead and feed ground defects and on-orbit anomalies into later builds.

**What we are looking for**
===========================

* 8+ years in quality engineering or quality management for aerospace, defense or similarly complex hardware, including 3+ years directly leading engineers, inspectors or specialists through production and test.
* Experience building a usable QMS and leading teams through supplier escapes, nonconformances, root cause and corrective action.
* Independent judgment, strong technical communication and the ability to separate Engineering disposition from Quality release concurrence.
* Working knowledge of configuration control, risk-based inspection, process capability and cross-functional investigations.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, materials science, physics or a related technical field, or equivalent quality leadership experience in complex hardware.

**For U.S. Roles:** To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

**For U.K. Roles:** To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC).

**For Canada Roles:** Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR.

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Compensation Range: $180K - $230K

records.title: Senior Manager, Quality and Safety
records.description:
Site: Wentworth-Douglass Hospital

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

**Job Summary**

The Senior Manager, Quality and Safety is responsible for leading the local execution of Mass General Brigham Community Division strategy, infrastructure, processes, and performance improvement efforts across patient safety, risk management, quality, and clinical compliance. This role oversees and supports the implementation of standardized best practices, safety and quality programs, regulatory readiness activities, and performance improvement initiatives that advance safe, reliable, high-quality care. 
 
The Senior Manager serves as a key local administrative leader and partners closely with system and site leadership, clinical teams, the local ACMO, risk/safety leaders, infection prevention, compliance, legal, data and analytics teams, and other stakeholders to execute both short- and long-term goals for Quality, Patient Safety, Risk Management, and Clinical Compliance programs. 
 
This position is responsible for translating system strategy into local execution while also providing strong bidirectional communication between the site and system teams regarding local risks, emerging trends, operational needs, performance gaps, and improvement opportunities. 
 
Because this is a leadership role in an active change-management environment, the Senior Manager must demonstrate flexibility, sound judgment, collaboration, and openness as the scope and needs of the role continue to evolve over time. 
 
Essential Functions 
 
Quality, Safety, and Risk Strategy Execution 
 

* Execute MGB Community Division strategy for patient safety, risk management, quality, and clinical compliance at the local site, ensuring alignment with standardized system processes, priorities, policies, and performance expectations.

 

* Support the buildout of local safety, quality, risk, and compliance infrastructure, including standardization in training, workflows, governance, reporting structures, and response processes that are in line with MGB.

 

* Collaborate with system and site leadership to execute long- and short-term goals for Quality, Patient Safety, Risk Management, and Clinical Compliance programs.

 

* Provide essential input to MGB leadership regarding strategy, infrastructure, policy development, performance improvement plans, and local operational needs to support high-quality care delivery.

 
Patient Safety and Risk Management 
 

* Execute MGB patient safety plans, including safety event reporting, event analysis, mitigation planning, and follow-up on safety-related concerns.

 

* Implement standardized risk management strategies, policies, and procedures, ensuring that risk management activities align with and strengthen the organization’s approach to patient safety.

 

* Implement and support use of the systemwide safety event reporting system.

 

* Support systemwide and local safety events, including recalls, shortages, and other issues that may impact patient safety.

 

* Partner with site Risk/Safety/PFR leaders and clinical teams to develop prospective solutions and performance improvement actions in response to safety events.

 

* Leads the development and delivery of patient safety and risk management training using culture‑of‑safety data, safety event trends, and systemwide priorities to promote continuous improvement, staff engagement, and safe, reliable care practices across all departments.

 

* Completes, within three (3) months of hire, High Reliability Organization (HRO) training, including Level 3, Fact Gatherer, and Process Facilitator, and integrates HRO principles into oversight of safety event analysis, improvement strategy, and organizational learning.

 
Quality Performance and Improvement 
 

* Serve as the local administrative leader responsible for executing quality performance and improvement programs at the site.

 

* Ensure adherence to MGB standardized processes for quality measurement, prioritized quality goals, quality strategy, and performance improvement activities.

 

* Provide proactive and reactive quality performance improvement planning in partnership with local clinical teams, department leaders, and floor-based teams.

 

* Lead the planning, implementation, and evaluation of process changes and performance improvement activities.

 

* Effectively communicate goals, strategic priorities, accountability expectations, and improvement plans to clinicians and operational leaders, engaging them as partners in achieving quality and safety outcomes.

 

* Serve as the senior local site manager responsible for Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) planning, documentation, and updates for board quality committee and/or patient care assessment committee needs.

 
Clinical Compliance and Regulatory Readiness 
 

* Serve as the senior local administrative manager responsible for clinical compliance activities, including tracer activity, site preparedness, monitoring, and adherence to standardized compliance processes.

 

* Build and support the local implementation of the MGB clinical compliance program, ensuring standardized processes, staff training, procedures, and governance are in place.

 

* Monitor institutional compliance with Joint Commission standards and other applicable regulations, and advise system leadership regarding areas requiring improvement.

 

* Lead or support proactive and reactive clinical compliance activities, including risk assessments, improvement plans, regulatory interpretation, and implementation of needed process changes.

 

* Serve as the senior clinical compliance manager responsible for management and performance during expected and unexpected regulatory visits, including but not limited to The Joint Commission, DPH, DMH, and CMS.

 

* Oversee submission of required documentation and reports to relevant accrediting and regulatory bodies, including DPH, DMH, TJC, BORIM, and MedSUN, and complete submissions directly when front-line support is not available.

 

* Liaise with system and site teams, clinicians, corporate compliance, and the Office of General Counsel regarding compliance issues, regulatory requirements, site visits, and areas of overlap.

 
Data, Analytics, Reporting, and Dashboards 
 

* Partner with MGB data and analytics teams to ensure reporting to CMS, other regulatory bodies, private payer contracting entities, external benchmarking organizations, and quality/safety reporting programs is timely and accurate.

 

* Understand data provided by system teams and use knowledge of local practices and culture to identify opportunities for improvement, emerging risks, and areas requiring local or system-level attention.

 

* Advise in the development of local and system-level dashboards related to quality performance, clinical compliance, patient safety, and improvement priorities.

 

* Analyze trends and emerging risks, communicate findings to local teams and system leaders, and support improvement planning based on available data.

 

* Prepare reports and presentations as needed for site leadership, system leadership, regulatory bodies, committees, and other stakeholders.

 
Collaboration and Local Leadership 
 

* Partner with the local ACMO and clinical teams to implement system goals, site-level improvements, and accountability processes.

 

* Liaise with infection prevention and control teams to monitor performance, respond to data, and support actions to reduce risk of infections to patients.

 

* Maintain strong organizational relationships and work effectively within a matrixed healthcare environment.

 

* Provide strong bidirectional communication between the system and site, including distribution of pertinent data, analytics, priorities, concerns, and operational feedback.

 

* Ensure recommended improvements are implemented and partner with local leadership to support accountability.

 
Staff Management and Department Operations 
 

* Manage, supervise, and support assigned quality, safety, risk, and/or compliance staff, including recruitment, interviewing, training, orientation, remediation, and performance evaluation.

 

* Establish development plans for staff and support ongoing professional growth, role clarity, and accountability.

 

* Manage departmental operations and budget responsibilities as assigned, including fiscal planning and budgetary recommendations.

 

* Oversee local training and educational programs related to quality, safety, risk, and clinical compliance as needed.

* 3-5 years of experience leading process improvement and initiatives and managing teams required.
